title: See the Changing of the Guard at Martyrs' Shrine
excerpt: Hourly changing of the guard at the Martyrs’ Shrine, commemorating 400,000 fallen soldiers. Ceremony times and how to get there.
searchText: see the changing of the guard at martyrs' shrine hourly changing of the guard at the martyrs’ shrine, commemorating 400,000 fallen soldiers. ceremony times and how to get there. visit buildings free the national revolutionary martyrs' shrine was built in 1969 to commemorate the loss of almost 400,000 taiwanese soldiers who lost their lives in a number of wars during the 20th century. the memorial archway gate is guarded throughout the day by two military personnel who, much like the guards at the chiang kai-shek and sun yat-sen memorial halls, will stand motionless and expressionless for their full hour on duty. every hour on the hour, from 09:00 until 17:00 , the changing of the guard ceremony will take place. an impressive feat of controlled and synchronised body and rifle movements. the ceremony will last around 20 minutes, with the new guards making a lengthy march from the main palace building before beginning their routine with the existing guards, who will make their exit to the right of the archway. the arch marks the entrance to a huge 22 hectare site featuring a large open area with gardens. at the other end of the site is the palace, which houses the spirit tablets of the 400,000 people who were killed over a period of around half a century. large tablets depicting scenes from some of the battles which took place over this period reside within the entrance to the palace. one depicting the battle of shanghai and the other guangzhou uprising, which ended the regime of the qing government and saw the birth of the republic of china. unfortunately, entry inside the p

excerpt: Thai food at genuinely competitive prices, five minutes north of City Hall MRT — cheaper than Taipei's other Thai spots.
searchText: cheap but tasty thai food at thai elephant thai food at genuinely competitive prices, five minutes north of city hall mrt — cheaper than taipei's other thai spots. eat restaurants thai whilst there are some great thai restaurants in taipei, none of those we've so far been to have been on the cheap side. thai elephant (chinese name: 象廚泰式料理), found 5 minute north of the city hall mrt, offers some great thai cuisine at very competitive prices. as we walked into the fairly basic restaurant, our nostrils were immediately hit with the fragrances we come to associate with thai cuisine. we were seated and were told we had a 90 minute dining time. not a problem, so long as they serve the food on time. thai elephant's menu is mainly in chinese, although they do have pictures. all the usual thai fare is here, with thai curries, pad thai, spicy minced pork etc. as it was our first time here, we played it safe and chose a few of our regular thai dishes. first up, the shrimp pancakes . these are always a good test to determine what the rest of the food will be like. very thick and juicy pieces, and they tasted just right! good start to the meal. next up, the thai green chicken curry , and a couple of portions of rice to go with it. again, it was exactly how i like my thai curries, fragrant and creamy, and the chicken pieces were perfect. another big tick. another main we chose was the minced pork with lettuce . the portion of mince we got was huge, although we only got 2 lettuce leaves to go with it, but it was nicely spicy and certainly filled us up. we also ordered a sid

title: Taiwan Science Education Center: Sky Bike & More
excerpt: Six floors of hands-on science plus the Sky Bike that runs on a rail three storeys up. Ticket prices and what suits which ages.

excerpt: The American steakhouse chain has two branches in Taipei, one near the airport in Songshan. How the steaks compare to the US original.

title: Comforting Indian Food at Oye Punjabi
excerpt: A small, authentic Indian restaurant in Dunhua, run by Indian expats sharing dishes from home.
searchText: comforting indian food at oye punjabi a small, authentic indian restaurant in dunhua, run by indian expats sharing dishes from home. eat restaurants indian oye punjabi is a small indian restaurant found in the dunhua area of taipei which packs a punch when it comes to authentic indian flavours and spices. like all the best indian restaurants found in this city, it's run by indian expats who have a desire to share their beloved cuisine with the rest of the world. oye punjabi only has enough room for 20 diners or so but we luckily booked ahead to ensure a seat. the staff are very attentive, and will ensure you have a good variety of dishes and will even choose a suitable level of spiciness for you. their menu is by no means huge, but there's a good range of curries, kebabs, vegetables, sides and rice/bread. to start, we chose the machli tikka , a tandoori fish marinade with chilli, cumin & coriander. the fish was flake-in-the-mouth soft and the marinade was a beautiful mix of spices. it was very spicy, but in a good way. good job we ordered a mango lassi to keep the heat at bay! silky smooth and very mango-ey. i was extremely happy to see they had a couple of dal dishes too, as i love lentils, and indian restaurants always seem to do them justice. the yellow dal tadka was everything i hoped for. warm and comforting, the lentils were soft but not overcooked. i could have just eaten a huge bowl of this, but we had a curry to get through. many of the curries here are fish-based, and since we had this as a starter, we chose the butter c

excerpt: A Taiwanese-style izakaya serving Taiwan craft beer, rather than the Japanese imports most izakayas stick to.

title: Great Hong Kong Cuisine at Dim Dim Sum
excerpt: A respected Hong Kong dim sum chain now in Taipei, tested against the original HK branches by someone who's eaten both.
searchText: great hong kong cuisine at dim dim sum a respected hong kong dim sum chain now in taipei, tested against the original hk branches by someone who's eaten both. eat restaurants  dim dim sum is a respected and established hong kong restaurant chain that has since opened up a couple of branches in taipei. having been fortunate enough to try dim dim sum in hong kong, we were so bowled over by the experience, we simply had to try the food in taipei to see how it compared. dim dim sum has been featured in a couple of publications including the world chefs global diet guide and also gained a place in the 101 best places to eat in the world . in fact, you'll be hard pressed to miss this fact, as they proudly display it all over the restaurant. now of course they serve hong kong's most famous export dim sum, but one of the dishes we tried and loved in hk and simply had to try here were the crispy shrimp . as the name suggests, they are crispy flour rice rolls filled with shrimp. now although they're crispy on the outside, they are much softer on the inside than traditional dim sum, and have a unique texture. dipped in soy, they are delicious and delightful mouthfuls. while i wouldn't say they were quite as up to the standard as those in hk, they are without question worth trying! another item from their menu i would strongly recommend are their pineapple buns with butter . these could actually pass as a dessert, but they're on the savoury menu so come out with the main meal, and are best eaten warm. they are incredibly light and the melting butter inside is in

excerpt: One of the best LPGA women's golf events in the world, held right on Taipei's doorstep. What to expect if you go.
searchText: taiwan lpga golf championship one of the best lpga women's golf events in the world, held right on taipei's doorstep. what to expect if you go. events live sports i've been fortunate enough to experience some world class golf tournaments before, having seen both the ryder cup and british open, but i've never seen a top class women's golf tournament. with one of the best lpga events in the world happening near this very city, i thought it would be rude not to give it a try. with a prize fund of over us$2 million, the 'swinging skirts' lpga championship, as it's known, attracts all the best female golfers in the world. this year, the miramar golf country club in linkou was hosting the event. as per most golf tournaments, it's held over four days, with the players taking the most shots being eliminated after day two. tickets are very reasonably priced at either nt$300 for the first couple of days, and nt$500 for the final two over the weekend. these can be purchases ahead of time from ibon machines (with discounts available if you have certain bank accounts), or directly before you enter the golf club. having never seen women's golf live before, i wasn't entirely sure what to expect. i knew that their game had vastly improved over the years, but i have to say that i was blown away by the quality. the only difference between the women's and men's games now are the power and the spin they're able to generate on the ball. the level of skill on display was easily up there with the men. in fact, i would say the miramar golf course was probably t

searchText: great gourmet sandwiches at liquid bread company (permanently closed)    permanent closure notice please note: liquid bread company has permanently closed. liquid bread company has been on my to-go list for a while now. there's nothing better than a well crafted hot sandwich, especially when it comes served with a nice cold beer. along with some great draft ales, they have a fantastic collection of bottled ales and soft drinks, many of which i've seen nowhere else in taipei. these cost from nt$200 to nt$260 and i almost bought one until i saw the draft ales. the liquid bread company restaurant is a very hip, urban and modern space. a mixture of stools and chairs, it's well lit and plays some great tunes. the atmosphere is lively, and pets are allowed - although i wished that dog would stop staring at me! some of the items on the menu were sold out. i'm not sure if this was a temporary thing or if they've simply stopped serving them. there were still plenty of choices available however, with blts, burgers and more traditional sandwiches. their bread is all made by purebread . if you know these, you'll probably know it's one of the best bakeries in taipei. so i was hoping for something extra special, and i have to say i wasn't disappointed. i went for the classic tuna melt . i wasn't actually sure the bread it was going to come with as it doesn't state on their menu. there is an option to change the type of bread you get for an extra nt$10. i know tha

title: See Fort San Domingo and Other Historical Buildings
excerpt: One NT$80 ticket covers Fort San Domingo and a cluster of historic buildings in Tamsui. What to see and how to reach them.
searchText: see fort san domingo and other historical buildings one nt$80 ticket covers fort san domingo and a cluster of historic buildings in tamsui. what to see and how to reach them. visit buildings museum walking fun pass located at the end of the red line in tamsui, fort san domingo is one of a whole cluster of historic buildings within a few minutes' walk of each other. some are ticketed, most are free, and it's worth knowing which is which before you go. a single nt$80 ticket from the tamsui historical museum covers three sites: fort san domingo , together with the british consulate residence in the same compound tamsui customs officers' residence , better known as the little white house hobe fort , a qing dynasty gun battery ten minutes further up the hill hobe fort is the one people miss. it's included in the ticket you have already bought, so there's no reason not to walk up. several more are free , including the former residence of tada eikichi and the tamsui customs wharf down at the water. and the buildings on the aletheia university campus – oxford college, the house of maidens and reverend mackay's residence – sit outside the museum ticket altogether, so don't expect it to get you through those doors. each has different opening hours, so if you are interested in seeing them all, it's best to visit between tuesday and thursday when they are all open. see opening hours section for further details. the oldest and most historically significant is fort san domingo , and its history is more tangled than the name suggests. the spanish built the original in 1628 and then tore it d

searchText: funky sounding ales at 23 public a taiwanese brewery's bar near shida night market, founded by two homebrew enthusiasts, known for its rotating chalkboard menu of ales and decent pub food. drink bars craft beer 23 is another taiwanese brewery that is slowly gaining prominence in taiwan. it was founded in 2014 by brett tieman and matt frazar, two taipei-based americans who met on a homebrewing course and wanted to bring american-style craft beer culture to the city. with their 23 public bars - located near shida night market - they are proving to be one of the best spots for a nice ale and decent grub. the city branch has a black board on the back wall serves as the ale menu, a pastiche of vibrant colours akin to a gasper noe title sequence. twelve crazy sounding ales, eleven of them brewed by 23 and one guest ale. my eyes were drawn to the mojohito, a lager mixed with pineapple and lime. not entirely sure why it was named as such, as there was no mint or rum involved. but it sounded fun so i gave it a go. a very summery drink - refreshing and zingy, it was a crisp clean lager that went down nicely. with other drinks including cucumber sour, passion fruit sour and heavy scotch ale, i'll probably try one of the flights next time, consisting of five smaller sized glasses. the bar is light and airy, with huge windows lapping up the sunlight, and it doubles up as a small record shop too, with crates of vinyl to flick through while you drink. 23 public is a good spot for a quick drink. i'll be back again to see if there food is any good too. menu price: $$$ level of english: good (english o

searchText: super salads and subs at hungry pans salads and subs that filled a real gap in taipei's food scene, back when good salad spots were genuinely hard to find. eat restaurants sandwiches healthy quick eats salads when i first came to taiwan i found it extremely difficult finding a good salad. maybe it was because i just didn't know of any good spots, or maybe it was because there weren't many places? in the last couple of years, a few good salad places have cropped up. hungry pans (which i can only assume is a pun of hunger pains) is one of the best and cheapest places to get your salad fix, while they also offer subway type sandwiches, pizzas and panini. they have three ranges of salads, the cheapest being simpler garden-based ones, the mid-range which includes meat such as chicken, turkey or ham, and the top-range with salmon, beef or chicken and bacon. these cost nt$110, nt$140 or nt$160 respectively. they also come with a choice of dressing included in the price. even though the ingredients are laid out in front of the counter, i don't believe you can choose specific items. hungry pans also have four combo deals available. i chose the basic one, with which you can choose a drink and dessert. i'm not exactly sure what the other combo deals are as they're not in english. black tea and the traditional taiwanese 'pudding'. for an extra nt$29, i thought it was a good deal. they'll give you a buzzer and you can grab one of the seats or stools. after what seemed like no time, the salad was ready. the grilled chicken salad came nicely presented in a wooden bowl, and i have to say it was a f

title: Admire the Beautiful Hsing Tian Kong Temple
excerpt: A working temple dedicated to Kuan Yu, and the first in Taiwan to ban incense entirely in 2014. What happens inside and how to take part respectfully.
searchText: admire the beautiful hsing tian kong temple a working temple dedicated to kuan yu, and the first in taiwan to ban incense entirely in 2014. what happens inside and how to take part respectfully. visit buildings free kuan yu is the primary deity worshipped at hsing tian kong temple, who possessed great loyalty and justice among men. the god has thus become as famous as confucius, and has also been honoured by the name kuan en zu - meaning saviour of the world. hsing tian kong temple was one of three built under the guidance of master hsuan kung (黃欉), a coal mine businessman turned devotee who personally funded all three and served as their first chief abbot. the beitou branch came first in 1960, followed by the sanxia xingxiu temple in 1965, with this main zhongshan district temple completed last, on 25th january 1968. people will come in their droves to pay their respect and ask for answers to important questions. by throwing divination blocks (two wooden objects with one flat side) onto the ground, they will pose a question that only requires a yes/no answer. how the blocks land will determine the answer: one lands flat side up, the other rounded side up - 'yes' answer both land rounded side up - 'no' answer both land flat side up - uncertain if the answer is uncertain, they will essentially throw again until a definitive answer is returned. look out too for the temple's shou jing (soul-calming) ritual, performed for free by volunteers in blue robes – mostly elderly women – usually between 11:20am and 6:30pm. it's meant to settle a person's spirit after a fright or a run of ba

title: Take a Walk Through the Bopiliao Historical Block
excerpt: A well-preserved Qing Dynasty street that was once one of Taipei's busiest passages. What survives today and how to see it.
searchText: take a walk through the bopiliao historical block a well-preserved qing dynasty street that was once one of taipei's busiest passages. what survives today and how to see it. visit buildings free walking sightseeing bus known today as kangding road, the bopiliao historical block is a well-preserved qing dynasty street which formed over 200 years ago as a key route between monga (modern-day wanhua) and guting. the name itself is a bit of a mystery. the popular story is that it comes from stripping bark off timber shipped in from fuzhou, or from an old hide-tanning pool – but neither has solid evidence behind it. the best-documented explanation is more mundane: old land deeds recorded the area as "bak-phoe-liau", and since that sounds almost identical to "bopiliao" in hokkien, the name likely just drifted into its current form over time. this made it one of the busiest and wealthiest areas in taipei, until japanese rule in the early 20th century displaced the street with newer roads. in 1941, the block was zoned as the future site of laosong elementary school, which froze it against redevelopment even as it fell into disuse – the very restriction that ended up preserving its mix of hokkien and western-style architecture. the taipei city government began renovating the area in earnest from 2003 until 2009, and it's become considerably more famous since – the 2010 gangster film monga, set in 1980s taipei, was shot on location here, and tourism has followed. current work is still going on, and they are extending the street with new buildings in the same style. many of the building

searchText: how and what to order at jin feng braised pork rice taiwan’s most famous braised pork rice, ten minutes from chiang kai-shek memorial hall. what to order, what it costs and when to go. eat restaurants local budget taiwanese top pick jin feng is one of the most famous and popular local restaurants in taiwan, whose speciality is braised pork rice dishes. located just a 10 minute walk from the chiang kai-shek memorial hall , jin feng braised pork rice is difficult to miss since there is almost always a large cluster of people on the street outside waiting to be seated. however, we managed to time it well (wednesday at 18:00), as it was the first time we've ever been able to walk straight in. otherwise, you could wait for up to 30 minutes. the staff will find a table for you (often shared with others), and give you a small slip for you to fill in your order. unfortunately, this is in chinese, but fortunately, you can ask for an english guide sheet with pictures (see menu section). you will still need to match the chinese text next to the picture with that on the slip, although it's far easier to match the price first. if you don't order the braised pork rice dish (which we once didn't), they'll look at you strange! it's on the menu as braised ground pork rice and comes in three sizes (小 - small, 中 - medium, 大 - large). it's essentially a bowl of rice with some braised pork on top and a piece of bitter melon, but it is delicious. make sure you mix it well before eating. we find the best dishes to accompany this are the boiled vegetables, which is usually water spinach - on the menu as cooked veggie and/or dried

title: Contemporary Izakaya at Range Bistrokaya
excerpt: A bistro-izakaya hybrid near Taipei City Hall, serving cocktails and small plates from an open kitchen.
searchText: contemporary izakaya at range bistrokaya a bistro-izakaya hybrid near taipei city hall, serving cocktails and small plates from an open kitchen. eat restaurants cocktails range bistrokaya, as the name suggests, is a cross between and bistro and izakaya restaurant, serving cocktails and small plates of food. situated close to the taipei city hall, the establishment is cosy and nicely fitted out, with an open kitchen where you can watch the skilled chefs preparing and cooking one of the many dishes available. you'll typically need to order 5 or 6 dishes for two people. they have a number of beef dishes available, with the more premium wagyu beef or diced beef premium , which we tried and was succulent and one of the best beef dishes we've tried in taipei. their fish dishes are equally as nice, with the mouthwatering prawns , squid, salmon, scallop and cuttlefish, or you could opt of a seafood combo comprising of all of the above. we also tried the mozzarella sticks with pork - they too were exceptional. in fact, all the dishes we tried looked and tasted amazing. you'll probably need to order 5 or 6 dishes to satisfy two people's hunger. we chose the pork shoulder and smoked salmon salad , with a lovely yellow mustard sauce. you can often tell how good the cocktails are likely to be be the choice of spirits behind the bar, and range bistrokaya have only high quality spirits - not a bell's whiskey or gordon's gin in sight. their house special cocktail , which is a mixture of beer, vodka and gin was very strong but with a deep multi-layered flavour.

title: Visit the Idyllic Shuangxi Park and Chinese Garden
excerpt: A compact but richly detailed Chinese garden in Shilin - rockeries, a moon bridge and a thundering waterfall, named for the twin creeks that meet nearby.
searchText: visit the idyllic shuangxi park and chinese garden a compact but richly detailed chinese garden in shilin - rockeries, a moon bridge and a thundering waterfall, named for the twin creeks that meet nearby. visit parks nature gardens free if you have a penchant for beautifully landscaped gardens, shuangxi park and chinese garden will be right up your alley. the name comes from the confluence of the wai shuangxi (outer twin creek) and nei shuangxi (inner twin creek) rivers nearby – "shuangxi" literally means "twin streams" – and despite what the name suggests, it's a proper chinese garden, not open parkland. built in 1974 and laid out by landscape architect hu guoli in a southern chinese courtyard style, it packs a lot into just 2 hectares (about 5 acres): rockeries, zigzagging pathways, caves, ponds, a moon bridge and a thundering waterfall. look out for the grey octagonal orchid pavilion near the entrance, modelled on the original orchid pavilion in shaoxing, china – the same pavilion that inspired the design of zhishan garden across town. it's a 15-minute walk from shilin mrt, which keeps it well off the typical tourist route – you'll usually have the winding paths mostly to yourself. its only real drawback is that it straddles two busy roads, so some traffic noise is unavoidable. aside from that minor quibble, the landscaping is second to none – shuangxi park and chinese garden is without question one of the nicest gardens to visit in taipei. opening hours open 24 hours a day, admission is free traveller tips take some drinks with you – there's little in the way of amenitie

title: Enjoy the Peace and Beauty at Zhishan Garden

searchText: enjoy the peace and beauty at zhishan garden a 5-acre chinese garden at the foot of the national palace museum steps, styled after the sung and ming dynasties, with carp-filled ponds. visit parks nature budget gardens sightseeing bus zhishan garden is a beautiful chinese garden at the base of the steps leading up to the national palace museum in shilin. it was designed and built by the taipei fine arts museum specifically to bring the feel of a traditional eastern garden closer to the public. reflecting the styles of the sung and ming dynasties across around 5 acres (1.88 hectares), it's laid out around eight named scenic spots inspired by the writings of wang xizhi, the famous chinese calligrapher – among them the orchid pavilion, songfeng pavilion and pen washing pool. three ponds filled with carp are threaded together by bridges and pathways, with three wooden pavilions dotted around for you to sit and take it in. if you find yourself at the national palace museum, zhishan garden is a must-visit – especially since it's free to enter with a museum ticket. price nt$20 (you'll need two nt$10 coins handy) free to enter with a national palace museum ticket opening hours 08:30 - 18:30 closed on mondays traveller tips drinks machines are located within the garden. it's not situated near an mrt station, so it's really only worth the detour if you're already visiting the palace museum. location see the national palace museum post for details on getting here

title: Tasty Scallion Pancakes at Lin's Chinese Pizza

searchText: tasty scallion pancakes at lin's chinese pizza scallion pancakes, not pizza despite the name, right next to shilin mrt — handy before the night market opens. eat stalls local budget taiwanese quick eats you've probably guessed already that these aren't pizzas – they're scallion pancakes, a doughy mix with scallion, filled with egg and flavoured with fresh basil. lin's is one of the best stalls in the area to try them, and sits right next to shilin mrt station, making it a handy stop if the night market hasn't opened yet and you're feeling peckish. the pancake is cooked fresh to order on a flat griddle right at the stall – a quick, satisfying thing to watch while you wait, especially if it's your first time seeing one made. they don't serve many varieties, but you can add cheese and chilli sauce for a bit of heat, and it's cheap enough that it's worth getting two if you're hungry. it's a small, no-frills operation – the kind of stall that's clearly aimed at locals rather than tourists – and it's rated 4.4 stars on tripadvisor, one of the better options in the wider shilin area for this kind of quick street food. traveller tips you can add cheese for nt$10 extra. location 📍 closest mrt: shilin - red line exit 1

title: New Orleans Inspired Seafood at Shrimp Daddy

searchText: new orleans inspired seafood at shrimp daddy  eat restaurants seafood shrimp daddy is a great little restaurant near songshan cultural park serving shrimp and lobster dishes. inspired by restaurants from new orleans, it has many different takes on shrimp dishes but their most popular ones are the seafood bowls, containing shrimp or lobster marinated and mixed with clams, crab, mussels and octopus, with a choice of vegetables and sauces. you can choose the spiciness too, from mild the very spicy - we tried the shrimp, clams and mussels and chose a medium spiciness, which was at the upper echelons for the levels we can ensure! the bowls are packed with seafood, and the marinated shrimp are deliciously juicy and flavoursome. there is plenty to get through for 2 people, but be prepared to get your fingers very messy. they provide loads of napkins and have a large sink if the mess gets too much. for a little extra, you can purchase add ons such as a small salad and soup, although these were nothing special. if you don't fancy one of these bowls, there are plenty of other choices - gumbos, buns, even mac 'n' cheese with shrimp, and lots of side dishes. we opted for some onion rings, which in hindsight was probably a bad idea due to the amount of food we already needed to consume. if you fancy something particularly fresh, you can choose from one of the live lobsters they keep in the tank. i wouldn't say it's the fanciest place we've ever dined in, and

title: Stunning Dishes at BON Meingerda & Dumpling
excerpt: A Taiwanese restaurant known for meingerda, a slippery, tricky-to-eat local take on gnocchi, alongside classic dumplings.
searchText: stunning dishes at bon meingerda & dumpling a taiwanese restaurant known for meingerda, a slippery, tricky-to-eat local take on gnocchi, alongside classic dumplings. eat restaurants local taiwanese bon meingerda & dumpling is a taiwanese restaurant serving local dishes such as dumplings and taiwanese pasta. the dishes they are most famous for however, are meingerda - a taiwanese take on gnocchi. slightly more slimy in texture than gnocchi and consequently very difficult pick using chopsticks. the mushroom meingerda and pepper sauce is one of the most beautiful looking local dishes we've tried in taipei, vibrant in colour and sitting pristinely within the fine bowl it's served in. even though it's a vegetarian dish, the meingerda and mushrooms give it a meaty texture. the dried chilli sitting atop adds some zing. the tom-yam meingerda with seafood and pork is the most expensive dish on their menu but there are many delightful textures and tastes at play, giving the dish a surf 'n' turf feel. the clams meingerda with rice wine is another of our favourites. the dishes may look small but the bowls are deep, with many pieces of pasta hidden underneath. the meingerda dishes come in soup form too (although we've yet to try these) and have seafood, pork, vegetarian or chicken variations. the dumplings also come on their own or in a soup. the non soup versions can be purchased in quantities of 10, 15 or 20, and are filled with pork and either leek or cabbage. i can just about handle 15. there are a number of soups and side dishes too, with cucumber, vegetables, radish and many oth

title: Taipei East District: Where to Shop, Eat and Drink
excerpt: The East District area of Taipei is packed with independent shops, cafes, restaurants and bars.
searchText: taipei east district: where to shop, eat and drink the east district area of taipei is packed with independent shops, cafes, restaurants and bars. shop areas walking sightseeing bus perfect for independent shops cafes bars and restaurants the east district (known as dongqu by the locals), located only slightly east of the centre of taipei, is a vibrant and popular area to visit during the night or day. before ximending was developed into the shopping district it is today, the east district was the place to go for independent shops, cafes, restaurants and bars. in fact, while it doesn't have the flashing lights or pedestrianised streets of ximending, i believe it has a much wider range of shops, restaurants and bars. these are all located both north and south of zhongxiao east road between the zhongxiao fuxing and sun yat-sen memorial hall stations on the blue line. there are loads of cool independent shops selling everything from fashion, cosmetics, gadgets and gifts. as for restaurants, there are dozens to choose from, with a wide range of cuisine available. italian, spanish, greek, mexican, french, lots of great vegetarian/vegan places, and a wealth of asian cuisine. these won't be too busy during the week, but during weekend evenings there will often be queues to dine in popular restaurants. see my places of interests section at the end of this post to view all the places i recommend here some of the best bars in taipei can also be found in the east district. expat bars, cocktail bars, and even hair salons which double as bars. the district also has a m

title: Be Gulliver at the Miniatures Museum of Taiwan
excerpt: Over 200 miniature exhibits collected from across the globe over two decades, including the museum's famous through-the-window scenes.
searchText: be gulliver at the miniatures museum of taiwan over 200 miniature exhibits collected from across the globe over two decades, including the museum's famous through-the-window scenes. visit buildings museum kids fun pass the miniatures museum of taiwan is dedicated to all things miniature. with over 200 miniaturised exhibits, it's a mightily impressive and varied collection. the museum is located in the basement of a modern office building, which is easy to miss as there's only a poster on the wall giving away it's whereabouts. for over 20 years, the miniatures museum of taiwan has been collecting these miniature works of art from across the globe, with large proportion originating from europe. some of the best and most detailed pieces are the through-the-window scenes. a voyeuristic peek into the lives of others. the level of detail on everything is staggering. the furnishings, the working lights, and most impressively, even the postage-stamp sized paintings have been expertly hand painted. you can barely even tell just by looking at some the pictures that they are in fact tiny versions. the majority of the exhibits here are of buildings , from tudor and victorian english architecture, right through to castles and ruins of ancient rome. almost all of the pieces here are of a scale of 1:12. fantasy and fairy tales are well catered for, with pinocchio, jack and the beanstalk and fantastical scenes with dinosaurs. there's also a section devoted to dolls and toys, including toy cars. maybe not strictly miniatures, but impressive nevertheless. you can even purchase miniature bottles of booze from t

title: Ximending Outdoor Drinking Area: Bars & Prices
excerpt: One of the few places in Taipei to drink outdoors. Which bars are worth it, what drinks cost, and when the area gets busy.
searchText: ximending outdoor drinking area: bars & prices one of the few places in taipei to drink outdoors. which bars are worth it, what drinks cost, and when the area gets busy. drink bars cocktails outdoor seating lgbt taipei doesn't have many areas where you can eat of drink outside, probably due to the heat, rain and mosquitos, but if you do want to brave the elements and enjoy a drink in the open, the ximending outdoor drinking area is the best place to go in taipei. located directly behind the red house, the area includes several bars and a shared seating area, and is a popular hangout for the lgbt community. the bars in this area include karen bar sol bistro commander g-paradise casa bar some pink neon lighting and rainbows will give hints at the campness of the area, but for straight people it never feels like you're unwelcome. in fact, the opposite is largely true, as the bar staff are generally friendly, and not pushy like bar areas in other asian countries. drinks served here include standard lagers, and slightly more camp ones such as hoegaarden rose. many cocktails can be purchased here and they're actually not too bad. you can also rent shishas in some of the bars, which come with flavoured tobacco. many of the bars also serve food, although i would recommend eating in the main ximending area before you come here. you'll find far more interesting food there. during the summer months, the area has fans and vapour sprays to cool people down if the temperature is up. the ximending drinking area is a vibrant place over the weekend, and is the best place in taipei to enjoy a drink outs

title: 25 Best Things to Do on Yongkang Street: Food, Gifts & Old Taipei
excerpt: The 25 best things to do on Yongkang Street, from the original Din Tai Fung and sixty-year-old beef noodles to mango shaved ice, gift shops and the Japanese-era lanes behind it.
searchText: 25 best things to do on yongkang street: food, gifts & old taipei the 25 best things to do on yongkang street, from the original din tai fung and sixty-year-old beef noodles to mango shaved ice, gift shops and the japanese-era lanes behind it. shop areas free walking sightseeing bus perfect for street food & snacks desserts & shaved ice cafes & craft beer gifts and souvenirs japanese-era architecture overview yongkang street runs for about a kilometre through daan, and it packs more good eating into that distance than anywhere else in taipei. timeout named it the 4th coolest street in the world in 2022 – and the coolest in asia – which is a lot to live up to, but the mix earns it: the original din tai fung at one end, sixty-year-old beef noodles, shaved ice, tiny gift shops, and lanes of japanese-era wooden houses just behind. it isn't pedestrianised, so the pavements get tight at weekends, and the best of it isn't on the main street at all – the alleys running off it, mostly to the west, are where the cafes and small shops hide. yongkang park sits in the middle as somewhere to sit down with whatever you've bought. so rather than a wander, here are 25 things worth stopping for , grouped so you can eat your way along in order or skip to the shops and the old streets. everything is within about ten minutes' walk of dongmen mrt. when to go and how long to spend come tuesday to friday if you can. a lot of taipei closes on mondays, and weekends bring queues at every place worth queueing for. give it two hours for food and shops alone, or half a day if you're adding qingtian street and rongjin gorgeous time. street food & snacks 1. tian jin oni

title: Go Bargain Hunting at Gongguan Night Market
excerpt: A student-area night market with a Michelin-recommended gua bao stall among its evening food scene. What else is worth trying.
searchText: go bargain hunting at gongguan night market a student-area night market with a michelin-recommended gua bao stall among its evening food scene. what else is worth trying. visit markets free the gongguan area during the daytime has many shops and restaurants, and during the evening the night market adds loads of great food stalls and other stands selling an abundance of gifts, jewellery and clothes. while the market itself isn't huge, the combination of this and the established shops make this a great area to come for people looking for bargains or food. there are three food stands i would strongly urge you to try here: lan jia traditional taiwanese snack serves delicious gua bao – a soft bun filled with a mixture of pork belly. it's even recommended by the michelin guide ho's sweet potato balls are by far the best we've tried in taipei - so light and crispy, they melt in your mouth click each image to found out more you'll be hard pressed to miss these, since there are always long queues extending from each stand. a couple of other nice food stands i would recommend at the gongguan night market are the korean topokki (found close to ho's sweet potato balls), and the multi-coloured dumpling stand. if you've never tried it, topokki is a spicy stir-fried rice cake dish with egg and cheese, and the ones here are divine. the dumpling stand serves a large selection of many types of sweet and savoury dumplings filled with shrimp, curry, custard and many others. there are many other great restaurants and food places in the gongguan area that are not part of the night mark

title: Wander the Winding Alleys of Gongguan

searchText: wander the winding alleys of gongguan gongguan has many cheap shops and restaurants, and comes alive during the evening when the night market opens areas free walking perfect for bargain hunters restaurants and food stalls live music kids located on the green line in the southern part of taipei, gongguan is situated close to taiwan's largest university - ntu, and as such has the largest population of students in taipei. due to this, gongguan benefits from having some of the cheapest shops and restaurants found in taipei. there are many clothes shops, with a huge number of sportswear shops selling trainers at far cheaper prices found in shopping malls. for kids, there are plenty of amusement arcades, and a water park called road castle with water slides and pools. there are also a few music venues, the wall live house being the best of these, with live international underground acts of high calibre. the james joyce irish pub also usually has bands playing over the weekend, or you could just go for one of the best pints of guinness in taipei. click to read about the wall click to read about james joyce the streets and winding alleys at gongguan make it easy to get lost, especially at night when gongguan night market brings in many more visitors. click to read more about gongguan night market many of the night market stalls are open during the day. if you visit the above post, there are three really great stands i would urge you to visit. alternatively, there are a couple of small restaurants to grab some quick meals. yu poke has some fresh and

title: Try a Delicious Bao at Lan Jia Traditional Taiwanese Snack
excerpt: A 30-year-old Gongguan Night Market institution serving Bib Gourmand-listed gua bao, or 'tiger bites pig' - a lucky Taiwanese bun with a history behind its name.
searchText: try a delicious bao at lan jia traditional taiwanese snack a 30-year-old gongguan night market institution serving bib gourmand-listed gua bao, or 'tiger bites pig' - a lucky taiwanese bun with a history behind its name. eat stalls local budget taiwanese quick eats michelin guide found within the gongguan night market, lan jia (藍家割包) serves gua bao (割包) - a soft bun filled with pork belly and other delights. it's been running for around 30 years, starting out as an unassuming little cart in a lane off roosevelt road before building a loyal following among national taiwan university staff and students, and workers from the nearby taipower building. the stand is extremely popular as these are arguably the best gua bao found in taipei - they've even found a place on the bib gourmand selection in the taipei michelin guide . recommendations don't come much higher than that. gua bao itself has a name that literally means "cut bun" in hokkien, referring to how the flat steamed dough is folded over into a pocket. it's also known as "tiger bites pig" (虎咬豬), since the folded bun resembles a mouth biting into the pork – a shape that traditionally made it a lucky food to eat at the lunar new year, resembling a gold ingot. a soft, warm bun stuffed with marinated pork belly, peanut powder and coriander. i was initially sceptical about the presence of the peanut powder, but it adds a nice sweetness that gives the bun a deep and rich flavour. the pork belly has obviously been marinated for some time as it melts in the mouth. i'm not usually a fan of fatty meats, but the fat here has been cooked and rendered down to a texture that's palatable even for my mouth. yo

title: Delicious Snacks at Tian Jin Onion Pancake
excerpt: Widely considered Taipei's best scallion pancake stall, on Yongkang Street - the name literally means 'scallion grab-cake', for how the dough is torn while frying.
searchText: delicious snacks at tian jin onion pancake widely considered taipei's best scallion pancake stall, on yongkang street - the name literally means 'scallion grab-cake', for how the dough is torn while frying. eat stalls local budget taiwanese quick eats tian jin onion pancake (天津蔥抓餅) is a food stall that's found on the famous yongkang street, just down the lane from yong kang beef noodles – and widely considered the best scallion pancake stall in taipei, if not all of taiwan. they're not actually onion pancakes though, as the translation is lost slightly here. there are scallion (similar to spring onions) pancakes - a fried doughy mix infused with scallion, a very popular dish especially at breakfast time. the chinese name, cong zhua bing, literally means "scallion grab-cake" – a reference to how the dough is scrunched and torn by hand as it fries, which is what gives it those flaky, chewy layers. the pancakes are fried to a golden crisp and then beaten to make them as light as possible, all prepared by a team of experienced aunties who keep the long queue moving quickly. you can have them on their own, although you'll find them a bit dry without any fillings, of which you have a few choices - egg, cheese, sweetcorn and ham or a mixture of these. prices run from around nt$25 for a plain one up to nt$60 for the works. we opted for the corn, cheese and egg one and it was very tasty! you'll need to find a good spot to eat them as there are no tables here, and they are very messy things. they don't supply napkins so make sure you have something to wipe your hands after! queuing is likely here, but you won't need to que

title: Traditional Desserts at Shaved Ice Huaxi
excerpt: A shaved ice stall in Huaxi Night Market dating back to around 1920, serving locals and TV crews alike for over a century - no English menu, all charm.
searchText: traditional desserts at shaved ice huaxi a shaved ice stall in huaxi night market dating back to around 1920, serving locals and tv crews alike for over a century - no english menu, all charm. eat dessert shops  tucked into huaxi night market , this local shaved ice and fruit smoothie stall is one of the oldest of its kind in taiwan, established around 1920. wanhua is taipei's oldest district, and longshan temple has been drawing crowds here for centuries – shaved ice vendors have been setting up nearby to serve temple-goers and market crowds for just as long, and this is one of the few still going from that era. very popular with the locals, it made its name over the years, featuring on many tv shows to help spread the word of its shaved ice desserts. the menu is only in chinese, so it's difficult to identify the many variations of shaved ice available, but we opted for their signature dish, which features a couple of types of beans, taro and glutinous rice and costing only nt$120. you'll probably need to point and hope you pick something you like – there's no english on the menu or among the staff, but that's part of the charm. they also offer blended fruit drinks which are equally as nice. if you're in huaxi night market or indeed longshan temple and are in need of some light and delicious refreshment, then look no further! location 📍 closest mrt: longshan temple - blue line exit 1 the restaurant is not on google maps but it's located on the left side as you're walking from longshan temple, somewhere around here.

title: Shaved Ice Heaven at Snow Bro
excerpt: A Da'an shaved ice spot worth going back to - classic and milky shaved ice, tonnes of toppings, and a Taiwanese peanut soup worth trying too.
searchText: shaved ice heaven at snow bro a da'an shaved ice spot worth going back to - classic and milky shaved ice, tonnes of toppings, and a taiwanese peanut soup worth trying too. eat dessert shops taiwanese snow bro (秘方雪人兄弟) is a taiwanese dessert place in da'an serving a variety of shaved ice dishes – the kind of spot people go back to more than once on the same trip. i'm only aware of a couple of branches located in the daan district but there could well be more. you can buy either classic shaved ice or a milky version mixed with condensed milk that is more fattening but delicious. there are tonnes of toppings available, with the classic mango or other fruit toppings such as berries, or a variety of beans, lotus seeds or even oreo, plus a few syrup options – including the more traditional longan syrup alongside the milkier condensed-milk version. if you're after something warm instead, their taiwanese peanut soup is also worth trying, from nt$65 with one topping up to nt$85 with three. you just need to make sure you don't eat them too quickly, as brain-freeze will often kick in! snow bro's shaved ice dishes are some of the best we've tried in taipei. menu it's not a big place, so seating can be limited at busy times, but the shaved ice more than makes up for it – a large selection, very tasty, and mid-range priced. english is spoken reasonably well and the menu has english on it too. traveller tips mango shaved ice is a must try! location 📍 daan branch (closest mrt: daan - red/brown line exit 5)

title: 7 Shopping Malls with that 'Wow' Factor

title: Navigate the Campus at National Taiwan University
excerpt: Taiwan's most prestigious university, founded in 1928 as Taihoku Imperial University - its campus, open to the public, is home to Royal Palm Boulevard and the famous Fu Bell.
searchText: navigate the campus at national taiwan university taiwan's most prestigious university, founded in 1928 as taihoku imperial university - its campus, open to the public, is home to royal palm boulevard and the famous fu bell. visit buildings nature free museum walking the national taiwan university (ntu) is the largest and most prestigious university in taiwan. it has a huge campus that's open to the public to walk around. ntu campus map (click to enlarge) it was originally established by the japanese while they were occupying taiwan during the early 20th century - founded in 1928 as taihoku imperial university, the seventh imperial university in the empire of japan - so there are many buildings that have japanese architecture. it was handed over to chinese administration and renamed national taiwan university on 15 november 1945. to walk around the entirety of the roughly 115 hectare (1.15 km squared) campus at the national taiwan university takes a good few hours so you'll need your walking boots on, but it has many beautiful buildings and areas of natural beauty, plus there are a number of museums to visit: ntu agricultural exhibition hall ntu museum of anthropology ntu herbarium ntu heritage hall of physics ntu geo-specimen cottage ntu museum of zoology ntu insect museum they have differing visiting hours but generally open between 10:00 - 16:00 (some close for any hour at midday). most of the area is pedestrian only, so you'll not be bothered by the noise of traffic, and it's generally a very tranquil area to walk around, with lots of shaded areas and cafes to escape the sun for a while. look out for the fu bell along royal palm bouleva

title: Enjoy the View of Taipei 101 at Lobster Foods
excerpt: Lobster dishes with outdoor seating and Taipei 101 views, in the Xinyi shopping district.
searchText: enjoy the view of taipei 101 at lobster foods lobster dishes with outdoor seating and taipei 101 views, in the xinyi shopping district. eat restaurants outdoor seating seafood located within the xinyi shopping district, lobster foods serves a variety of interesting lobster dishes. with plenty of outdoor seating available and with great views of taipei 101, it's one of the best places to dine in the area if you prefer sitting outdoors. their main dishes are lobster rolls , for which you can buy with either a half or a full lobster's worth of meat. coming served in a soft brioche roll and topped off with some tangy salsa, they're a delight. for slightly extra, you can order a set, which comes with either chips or quesadillas, salad and a very good lobster chowder. alternatively, you can get a lobster risotto, lobster pizza, lobster pasta or a lobster burger. lobster foods also serves one of the best pints of guinness in taipei - they even have a certificate from guinness as proof. a very full bodied pint with the trademark creamy white head and black body. i too can certify that it was a damn good pint, easily up there with the james joyce guinness we tried in gongguan! lobster foods is in a very good location, situated in a nice part of xinyi with plenty of outdoor seating, and is a nice place to relax for a while. it's location does make lobster foods even more expensive than it would normally be however. it's certainly not cheap here, with a meal for two and drinks costing well in excess of nt$1,400. pros nice lobster outdoor seating great guinness

title: A Great Pint of Guinness at James Joyce Irish Bar
excerpt: An Irish chain bar with what might be the best pint of Guinness in Taipei — full-bodied with a proper creamy head.
searchText: a great pint of guinness at james joyce irish bar an irish chain bar with what might be the best pint of guinness in taipei — full-bodied with a proper creamy head. drink bars live music whiskey a capital city wouldn't be complete with an irish bar. james joyce is an irish chain you've probably heard of, and of course serves pints of ireland's most famous drink - guinness. and it's a damn good pint of guinness, full in body with a creamy head that goes down very smoothly. if guinness isn't your thing, they have a few other tapped beverages, including the very irish magner's cider and the not so irish carlsberg and taiwan beer. their shelves are also stocked to the brim with irish whiskeys, plus a large selection of other spirits from which they can make some basic cocktails. they have a nice selection of gins available too and make a mean gin 'n' tonic. they do however serve no food, although a pint of guinness could almost pass as a liquid meal. james joyce irish bar is cosy place with a few small tables by the bar and some some seating at the back, plus they have three tables outside. all in all, they is seating for around 40 people and it does get very busy after 8pm. in the corner is a small stage where they'll have bands playing genres such as folk (irish probably) and country. the bands usually only play on a saturday evening. james joyce irish bar is a small but great little pub that serves one of the best pints of tap guinness in taipei. menu pros very good pint of guinness live music at the weekend cons small no food available price: $$ level of english: good

title: Be Inspired at the Museum of Contemporary Arts
excerpt: A contemporary art museum inside a red-brick 1921 Japanese-era schoolhouse that later served as Taipei's City Hall - two floors of changing exhibitions near Q Square.
searchText: be inspired at the museum of contemporary arts a contemporary art museum inside a red-brick 1921 japanese-era schoolhouse that later served as taipei's city hall - two floors of changing exhibitions near q square. visit buildings art fun pass otherwise known as moca, the museum of contemporary art shows temporary art exhibitions, with a heavy emphasis on modern audio/visual art. situated close to the q square shopping mall, the red-brick building with its distinctive central clock tower dates back to 1921, when it was built as jiancheng elementary school under japanese colonial rule – designed by kondō jūrō, the same government architect behind several of the era's official buildings. after 1945 it served as taipei's city hall until the city government moved to xinyi in 1994, before being restored and reopening as a museum in 2001. unusually, it still shares its site with a working junior high school next door. there are usually a couple of exhibitions at any one time across its two floors, often with screens showing multimedia or interactive artwork – the art is interesting and often carries a strong message, though some of the audio doesn't come with english subtitles. the main room on the second floor usually hosts some impressive larger exhibits. the first time we went, they had a number of large projections that told a story from a different perspective on each screen. the most recent exhibition featured many interactive displays, one which painted your image as you moved and swayed. located on the first floor are other exhibits, a cafe and a gift shop with some eclectic items on sale. price nt$50 c

title: Tasty Drinks at Yaboo Cafe
excerpt: A quiet, student-friendly cafe tucked off Yongkang Street near Dongmen - pricier than most in the area, but a lovely spot to work or unwind.
searchText: tasty drinks at yaboo cafe a quiet, student-friendly cafe tucked off yongkang street near dongmen - pricier than most in the area, but a lovely spot to work or unwind. drink cafes outdoor seating yaboo (鴉埠咖啡) is a popular student friendly cafe tucked down a side street off yongkang street near dongmen, founded by sisters emily and tina tsai back in 2010. as with most cafes in the area, you'll pay above the average for beverages and food, but it's a nice place to unwind or work. it has a mellow vibe and is very quiet, while they provide indoor and outdoor seating (plus a basement floor for extra room), as well as the obligatory free wifi. they have a selection of teas and coffees available, including more unusual offerings such as banana tea, while some of their coffees have an alcoholic twist. yaboo have their own coffee bean grinder outside with many exotic beans to choose from. there's a selection of pasta dishes, otherwise you can opt for one of their very good cakes. the house cat can usually be found sleeping in it's comfy bed. yaboo cafe is a nice place to chill with a drink while you are in the dongmen area – just be prepared to pay a bit more than at other cafes nearby for the privilege. traveller tips if it's too busy here, their sister cafe yaboo ii is a few minutes' walk away on lishui street – a brighter, more work-friendly space, though i've not been myself. location 📍 closest mrt: dongmen (red line - exit 5)

title: See the Dinosaurs at the National Taiwan Museum

title: Take a Steamy Tour of the Beautiful Xinbeitou
excerpt: Xinbeitou is an area of natural beauty found in Beitou, and is most famous for its Hot Springs.
searchText: take a steamy tour of the beautiful xinbeitou xinbeitou is an area of natural beauty found in beitou, and is most famous for its hot springs. areas visit buildings parks nature free walking perfect for walking relaxing nature hot springs click to enlarge xinbeitou is an area of natural beauty found in the northern beitou district of taipei. due to the high amount of volcanic activity deep below the ground, it is most famous for its hot springs . having it's own dedicated mrt line, you can catch the xinbeitou mrt train by changing via the beitou station on the red line. it's just a 5 minute journey and a single stop away from here. steaming streams and pools run through the whole area, and the sulphur in the air is the first thing you'll notice stepping off the train. the walk from xinbeitou station to thermal valley will take you past many beautiful buildings and through the lovely beitou park . the beitou hot spring museum and beitou library are just two of the fine buildings you'll walk past, and both are open most days. there are numerous hotels around the streets, all taking advantage of the hot springs, many with private baths filled with the thermal spring water. klook.com if you fancy a dip in the spring water yourself, there are many foot spas located around xinbeitou. they are however quite strict on what you can wear, so ensure you take some appropriate swim wear with you! alternatively, you can find one of the hot spring sinks to test the waters for free. beitou hot spring museum set on the edge of beitou park, the museum explains how the springs formed

title: Fine Crafts and Gifts at The Red House
excerpt: A 1908 Japanese-era landmark next to Ximending, now housing craft stalls, a tea shop and a music venue. What to see and buy.

title: Huaxi Street Night Market: Taipei's Snake Alley Today
excerpt: Once famous for live snake shows, Huaxi Street Night Market near Longshan Temple is now a Michelin Bib Gourmand food street - the snake vendors closed for good in 2018.
searchText: huaxi street night market: taipei's snake alley today once famous for live snake shows, huaxi street night market near longshan temple is now a michelin bib gourmand food street - the snake vendors closed for good in 2018. visit markets free sightseeing bus right next to longshan temple in taipei's oldest district, wanhua, sits huaxi street night market – better known by its old nickname, snake alley . it was taiwan's first market built specifically for tourists, opening in 1951, and for decades it earned its name honestly: vendors would skin and kill live snakes on the street to draw a crowd, selling snake meat, snake wine and snake gallbladder as health tonics. that's all history now. snake performances were banned under taiwan's animal protection act in the 2000s, and the last snake restaurant on the street, asia snake meat store, closed for good in may 2018. if you've come hoping to see snakes, you're a few years too late – but what's replaced them is arguably more worth the trip. what's there now much of the market runs down a long, covered indoor section – unusual for a taipei night market, and a nice option if you're caught out by rain. alongside the usual night market food, you'll find dozens of cheap massage and nail treatment stands, a holdover from the street's earlier days as a red-light district before prostitution was outlawed in taiwan in 1991. the whole market was awarded a michelin guide bib gourmand in 2019, and one stall in particular has its own individual recognition: yuan fang guabao , which has been selling gua bao (steamed buns stuffed with marinated pork belly, pickles and ground peanuts)

title: Visit the Magnificent Longshan Temple
excerpt: Taipei's most famous temple, built in 1738 and rebuilt after wartime bombing. Over 100 deities, how to pray now incense is banned, and the best time to visit.
searchText: visit the magnificent longshan temple taipei's most famous temple, built in 1738 and rebuilt after wartime bombing. over 100 deities, how to pray now incense is banned, and the best time to visit. visit buildings top pick free sightseeing bus longshan temple is one of the oldest temples in taiwan, founded in 1738 by settlers from fujian and dedicated to guanyin, the goddess of mercy. it's been rebuilt more than once since – earthquakes have damaged it over the centuries, and it took a direct hit from us bombing during wwii, destroying much of the main hall. despite all that, it remains one of the most popular and impressive temples in taipei, drawing large crowds throughout the day. under one roof you'll find over 100 deities from a mix of buddhist, taoist and chinese folk traditions – alongside guanyin, look out for mazu (goddess of the sea), wenchang dijun (god of literature, popular with students before exams), the red-faced guan gong (god of war and business), and yue lao, the matchmaker god. yue lao in particular draws a steady stream of visitors praying for love, both local and foreign. how to pray one thing worth knowing before you go: longshan temple banned incense burning by visitors back in march 2020, on top of stopping the burning of paper "joss" money a few years before that (taipei's then-mayor announced the change at the temple in 2017, when the number of incense burners was also cut from seven to three). both moves were about air quality – the temple sits in a dense, built-up part of the city. these days, worshippers pray with their hands rather than lit incense, on the idea that a

title: Cheap Drinks and Snacks at Yolo's Cafe
excerpt: A cheap and cheerful Taiwanese cafe chain named for YOLO - good wifi, plug sockets, and a black tea for as little as NT$35.
searchText: cheap drinks and snacks at yolo's cafe a cheap and cheerful taiwanese cafe chain named for yolo - good wifi, plug sockets, and a black tea for as little as nt$35. drink cafes tea budget sandwiches yolo's cafe is a taiwanese chain named after the acronym yolo ("you only live once"), with a good selection of food and beverages at very reasonable prices – a black tea can cost as little as nt$35. the cafes are well decked out, with cool and funky styling, and are a good place to work as the wifi is generally good and they have plug sockets at most seats. serving mainly sandwiches, they have toasties, bagels, toasts and also burgers and hot dogs – the german hot dog burger with cheese and the cheese croissant with beef are among the more popular picks. they also have something called a mochi crispy sandwich, which i've not tried but i'm guessing is a dessert as it's filled with red beans, matcha or sweet potato. drinks include milk-based coffees such as lattes and mochas, drip coffees from around the world, and of course tea, with many fruit teas, twinings teas (their brown sugar milk tea is a favourite) and the usual green/black teas. yolos cafe is one of the cheapest and best places to visit for a nice drink or snack. just be aware some of the seating isn't the comfiest if you're planning to stay a while. traveller tips along with louisa , probably the best value for money cafe chain in taipei locations dunhua branch (zhongxiao dunhua mrt - exit 7) zhongshan branch (zhongshan junior high school mrt - exit 1) datong branch (minquan w. rd. mrt - exit 1)
