title: Travel Back in Time at the Lin Family Mansion
excerpt: An overlooked 19th-century mansion and garden once owned by one of Taiwan's wealthiest families — one of the best-preserved of its kind in Taipei.
searchText: travel back in time at the lin family mansion an overlooked 19th-century mansion and garden once owned by one of taiwan's wealthiest families — one of the best-preserved of its kind in taipei. visit buildings top pick gardens fun pass often overlooked by visitors to taipei, the ben-yuan lin family mansion is a beautiful and tranquil property with stunning gardens. formerly owned by a wealthy taiwanese businessman, this is one of the few (and probably the best) garden/mansions in taipei that has still retained many of it's original features. click to enlarge set behind a wall, stepping into the 5 acre property is like stepping into a time machine taking you back a hundred or so years. the buildings and gardens are all in exquisite condition, with many doors, corridors and paths leading you to areas even more beautiful than the ones before. the banyan shade pond at the front of the property is the largest and most impressive of the three, with paths and bridges winding around it, and turtles, ducks and carp also enjoying the peacefulness. over the years, the roots of the trees have become entwined with the walls and rocks within the property, giving you an ethereal and other-worldliness feeling as you walk around, while some out-buildings and paths have been cleverly built into the surrounding landscape. the beautiful grounds are a popular destination for wedding photography, and it's easy to see why. stunning gardens, pavilions, terraces, ponds and buildings which would make a great backdrop for any photo. the three-house courtyard to the east is largely a private property. ancestors of the the original lin f

title: Trendy and Tasty Brunches at Kuang's Bistro
excerpt: A brunch spot in Banqiao, 15 minutes from Taipei Main by MRT, in a cluster of a dozen or so brunch places worth the trip.
searchText: trendy and tasty brunches at kuang's bistro a brunch spot in banqiao, 15 minutes from taipei main by mrt, in a cluster of a dozen or so brunch places worth the trip. eat restaurants breakfast/brunch salads kuang's bistro is located in banqiao near a cluster of brunch and breakfast places. although it's a 15 minute mrt ride from taipei main, it's worth the journey as they provide one of the best brunches in taipei. even if you don't get a space here, there are at least a dozen other very good brunch options within walking distance. focusing on salads, panini, brioche and smørrebrød (a traditional scandinavian open-faced sandwich), they also have some smaller bruschetta bites available. the dishes can be vegetarian, or come with a choice of meat (pork, beef, salmon, crab, duck). they're immaculately presented and taste just as good, although the salad we had was slightly on the greasy side. the crab meat brioche , served on a bed of fresh vegetables and a side of crispy thyme potatoes and a dollop of creme fraiche. it looked stunning and tasted equally as good. being huge avocado fans, we opted for the avocado salad , with lettuce, radish, tomato and black olives, and a side of warm toasted fingers. although it was slightly greasy for our liking, all the ingredients were fresh and most importantly, the avocado was soft and delicious. we also chose a smoked salmon bruschetta to share. the bruschetta dishes are much smaller so it's advised not to get one of these as your only dish. simple but tasty with the salmon being the star. the drinks also look the business, the cold drinks ver

title: Find the Surprise in Ay Chung Flour Rice Noodles
excerpt: A single-dish stall in Ximending famous for its flour rice noodles and a queue that rarely lets up. Is the wait worth it?
searchText: find the surprise in ay chung flour rice noodles a single-dish stall in ximending famous for its flour rice noodles and a queue that rarely lets up. is the wait worth it? eat restaurants budget taiwanese top pick found within the ximending (ximen) district, ay chung is a famous and extremely popular stall that serves only one thing - flour rice noodles. it's tucked away down one of the alleys in ximending, but it's difficult to miss as there's almost always a huge queue of people, while others hang around to consume them. the good news is the staff have a very efficient production line, so the queue moves rapidly. coming in two sizes (costing nt$60 or nt$75 ), the noodles are very silky and the mixture runny. it's difficult to eat with the supplied plastic spoon, but the taste is deep and strong. the hint of basil adds a nice freshness to the taste. you can also order these via klook for only nt$54 and nt$70 respectively klook.com hidden within the mix is a surprise - salty cured pig intestines , which are very chewy and i found difficult to swallow. if you want to add a bit of spice or extra flavour, there are three condiments to choose from: pureed garlic chilli sauce vinegar as there are no tables, it's advised to eat them close to the store (it's considered rude to take them away). there is a food bin to dispose of leftovers, and other bins for the bowls and spoons. if you're in in the ximen area and want to give a local delicacy a try, ay chung flour rice noodles is a must visit! pros the best flour rice noodles in taipei busy but queue goes down fast cheap cons can you handle the

title: See the History of the Taipei Story House
excerpt: Taiwan's only Tudor-style heritage building - a 1913 guesthouse turned prison turned legislator's home, now a small free museum next to the Fine Arts Museum.
searchText: see the history of the taipei story house taiwan's only tudor-style heritage building - a 1913 guesthouse turned prison turned legislator's home, now a small free museum next to the fine arts museum. visit buildings free museum sightseeing bus the taipei story house is a small faux-tudor house and museum right next door to the fine arts museum – and it's the only tudor-style heritage building in taiwan, which alone makes it an odd, interesting little detour. it was built in 1913–1914 during the japanese colonial era by chen chao-chun, a wealthy tea merchant, as a guesthouse for dignitaries and business associates. its history since has been anything but quiet: it was used as a prison and detainment centre in the later years of japanese rule, then became the private residence of huang kuo-shu, a speaker of the legislative yuan, in the 1950s. it was named a heritage site in 1998, restored by the taipei fine arts museum from 2000, and reopened as a small museum in 2003. inside, look out for the two original fireplaces and art nouveau tiles featuring natural and floral patterns. it now hosts rotating exhibitions, workshops and occasional traditional tea ceremonies, so what's actually on show will vary by the time you visit. it's not really worth a special trip on its own, but it sits near a few other attractions worth combining it with, or you could see it as part of a walk i've devised. opening hours 10:00 - 17:30 closed on mondays and during national holidays price free traveller tips see this as part of a walk . location 📍 closest mrt: yuanshan station (red line - exit 2)

title: Visit the Zones of the Collective Botanical Garden
excerpt: Officially the Future Pavilion, a leftover greenhouse from the 2010 Taipei International Flora Expo - smaller than the main Botanical Garden, but a wider range of plants indoors.
searchText: visit the zones of the collective botanical garden officially the future pavilion, a leftover greenhouse from the 2010 taipei international flora expo - smaller than the main botanical garden, but a wider range of plants indoors. visit parks nature gardens free the smaller of the two botanical gardens located in taipei, the collective botanical garden does however have a much wider range of plants, since it's mainly located inside, with climate controlled zones featuring flora from around the world. it's officially known as the future pavilion (未來館), one of the buildings left over from the 2010 taipei international flora exposition, and now sits inside xinsheng park within the wider taipei expo park – the same park that's home to maji square. it's also certified as a diamond-level green building, the highest tier in taiwan's green building rating system. the zones found inside are tropical subtropical temperate succulents alpine as you walk through the huge greenhouse, you'll start off in the tropical climate and walk through each of the zones. tropical - high temperature, high humidity with mainly flora found in rain-forests. subtropical - making use of taiwan's native trees and shrubs to create a rich plant ecology. temperate - grasses, conifers, deciduous trees and temperate fruit trees succulents - desert plants, with over 500 succulent plants including many cacti. alpine - plants found over 3,500 meters in altitude able to withstand cold temperatures there's also a beautiful outdoor section devoted to native flora, with flowers, plants and a pond full of lilies. the collective botanical garden was virtually empty when i loo

title: Visit the Beautiful Lin An Tai Ancestral House
excerpt: One of Taiwan's oldest buildings, dating to 1785 - dismantled and rebuilt at its current site after a preservation campaign that helped shape national heritage law.
searchText: visit the beautiful lin an tai ancestral house one of taiwan's oldest buildings, dating to 1785 - dismantled and rebuilt at its current site after a preservation campaign that helped shape national heritage law. visit buildings gardens free an exquisite and very well maintained house and gardens found in the northern part of the city, the lin an tai ancestral house dates back to 1785, making it one of the oldest buildings in taiwan. the lin family named it "an tai" in honour of their ancestral home, anxi county in fujian, and rong tai, the family business that paid for it. there are five buildings within the grounds, built in the southern fujian courtyard style with distinctive upturned swallowtail roof ridges, and you're free to explore inside the houses (although there was a wedding reception during my visit so i never got to see inside). a useful english guide to the buildings can be found here . the beautiful landscaped gardens and pond look stunning, and there are walkways and pavilions to explore. look out for the large weathered rocks scattered around the front courtyard too – they started out as ballast on chinese merchant ships and were repurposed once they'd served their purpose at sea. the house hasn't always stood here. it originally sat on siwei road in da'an district, but was threatened with demolition in 1978 to make way for the widening of dunhua south road. the campaign to save it drew in scholars and local artists, and is widely credited as a catalyst for taiwan's 1982 cultural heritage preservation act. the whole building was carefully dismantled and rebuilt piece by piece at its current r

title: Taipei Fine Arts Museum: Tickets & What's On
excerpt: Taiwan's first modern art museum, opposite Expo Park. Current exhibitions, ticket prices and how long to allow.
searchText: taipei fine arts museum: tickets & what's on taiwan's first modern art museum, opposite expo park. current exhibitions, ticket prices and how long to allow. visit buildings budget art sightseeing bus fun pass located just over the road from the expo park, the fine arts museum is the best place to visit if contemporary/modern art is your thing. opened in 1983, it became the first modern art museum in taiwan - and is arguably still the best. showcasing contemporary chinese and international art, the building itself is a striking piece of geometric art. there are four levels, with the 2nd floor dedicated to chinese art and sculptures, and the basement and 3rd floor rotating a number of exhibitions each year. source: https://www.tfam.museum the collections span many art-forms and styles, from traditional paintings, sketches and sculptures, to photography, installations and multimedia works. click here to see their current exhibitions the second floor is where you'll find the majority of the taiwanese exhibitions. works span the japanese rule period to the present day, and include contemporary art and those in more traditional styling. the 3rd floor also had many interesting and unique art works and sculptures, featuring both local and international artists. including some slightly more surreal concoctions. during my visit, there was a great audiovisual installation in the basement that involved the use of not only sound, but light and movement. many people come here just to work, as there's a library in the basement and a few areas to sit. the fine arts museum is a must visit attraction

title: Visit the Rose Garden and Maze at Xinsheng Park
excerpt: A 19.5-hectare rose garden and maze in northern Taipei, part of the former Flora Expo grounds, a five-minute walk from the Lin An Tai Ancestral House and the Collective Botanical Garden.
searchText: visit the rose garden and maze at xinsheng park a 19.5-hectare rose garden and maze in northern taipei, part of the former flora expo grounds, a five-minute walk from the lin an tai ancestral house and the collective botanical garden. visit parks nature free located in the north of taipei city, xinsheng park is a little out of the way but there are a couple of other attractions worth visiting while you are here. completed in 1978 and spanning 19.5 hectares, it's one of the largest parks in the city, and served as one of the four main exhibition areas for the 2010 taipei international flora exposition. the beautiful lin an ancestral house is just 5 minutes walk from the park, while the collective botanical gardens can be found within the park and features six climate zones - from tropical and alpine to succulent and orchid displays - showcasing around 500 plant species inside a diamond-level green building. click an image to read more about each xinsheng park also has a lovely rose garden, although you'll only find it in bloom during the spring months. the best time to see the roses is during march and april . there are hundreds of rose species in full bloom during these periods - over 700 varieties across more than a hectare of the park, making it the largest free rose garden in taiwan. the garden maze is a good place for kids to run around, although the low height of the hedges does make it a challenge when it comes to hiding. it's actually split into two separate mazes - a taller, trickier one for adults and a shorter one for younger children - laid out around a design loosely inspired by the yin-yang and five elements of traditi

title: Kooky Western Meals at Kooks
excerpt: A husband-and-wife run western restaurant tucked in the alleys of Tamsui, with an artwork-covered interior and a Pulled Pork Burger worth the trek for.
searchText: kooky western meals at kooks a husband-and-wife run western restaurant tucked in the alleys of tamsui, with an artwork-covered interior and a pulled pork burger worth the trek for. eat restaurants western vegan/vegetarian salads it's a pity that kooks (異嗑堂) don't have any restaurants located close to taipei city, as i'm sure i would be a regular visitor. located in the northern district of tamsui, it was opened by husband-and-wife team liam mcdonagh and emma chen, and serves fantastic western meals. kooks serve some great western dishes, and have an extensive menu that includes wraps, burgers, sandwiches, salads and pasta. they also have a large range of mexican and middle eastern cuisine and many vegetarian dishes, and are happy to adapt dishes to be vegetarian on request. their interiors are bright and bold, seating around 30 people, with the walls covered in liam's own original artwork alongside retro pictures and photos. there's a range of books and films for you to browse too. it is indeed very kooky. when i first came here, i honestly wasn't expecting a great deal from their food. but kooks burgers, especially their pulled pork burger , was up there with the best i've tried in taipei. the drinks too are varied and delicious – milkshakes, smoothies, a good range of teas, and a small but decent selection of beers and cocktails. if you are in tamsui, it's only a short walk from the mrt station there. kooks serve probably the best western food in the district, and it's usually not busy either – just be aware it's a bit of a trek from central taipei. traveller tips definitely worth checkin

title: Visit the Tranquil Dalongdong Baoan Temple and Gardens
excerpt: A beautifully constructed temple across the street from Confucius Temple, built by clan members generations ago. What to see and when to visit.
searchText: visit the tranquil dalongdong baoan temple and gardens a beautifully constructed temple across the street from confucius temple, built by clan members generations ago. what to see and when to visit. visit buildings gardens free situated just across the street from the confucius temple, the dalongdong baoan temple is another beautifully constructed building where you can watch (or join) people praying or asking the gods for advice. the temple's origins trace back to 1742, when settlers from tong'an in fujian carried incense from their hometown's ci ji temple to dalongdong and built a shrine to the baosheng emperor – a deified physician credited with a number of medical miracles, still worshipped today as a god of healing. construction of the current temple took decades and wasn't finished until 1830. like the confucius temple, it has some beautifully crafted detailing on the roofs and columns of the main structure. look closely and you'll spot a bit of friendly rivalry in the craftsmanship: during a 1917 renovation, two master carpenters, chen ying-pin and guo ta, were each given one side of the temple to decorate, competing to outdo each other's woodwork and carvings. a large-scale restoration in 1995 later earned the temple a 2003 unesco asia-pacific heritage award for culture conservation. located just over the road is the baoan temple garden , featuring a pond with a water feature and some miniature scenes. if you visit the dalongdong baoan temple around april to june, you'll witness the baosheng cultural festival , which features many parades and competitions celebrating the baosheng emperor

title: Be at One with Yourself at the Confucius Temple
excerpt: One of Taipei's most beautiful temples, demolished by the Japanese in 1907 and rebuilt by local gentry from 1925 - blending Qufu and southern Fujianese architecture.
searchText: be at one with yourself at the confucius temple one of taipei's most beautiful temples, demolished by the japanese in 1907 and rebuilt by local gentry from 1925 - blending qufu and southern fujianese architecture. visit buildings essential free top pick one of the most beautiful temples in taiwan, the confucius temple was originally built between 1879 and 1884, but was demolished by the japanese in 1907 to make way for what's now taipei first girls' high school, still operating on the original site today. it took until 1925 for a group of taipei gentry – among them chen pei-gen and koo hsien-jung – to donate around 5,000 ping (over 4 acres) of land at dalongdong and fund a full rebuild. construction began in 1927 under master craftsman wang yi-shun of quanzhou, with the main halls completed by 1930, though decorative work continued until 1939. combining the styles of the qufu confucius temple and southern fujianese architecture, it is a shrine to confucius, who has long been recognised for his unparalleled contribution to ancient chinese classical studies. the main building, the dacheng hall, is surrounded by a courtyard with side-buildings and is a beautiful peaceful place to walk around and admire – usually not busy, and a genuinely calm, peaceful spot despite being only a 10 minute walk from the closest mrt. many ornaments such as bells and drums adorn the courtyard and temples. you can try your hand at archery, or try the 4d theatre which shows two films in rotation about the life and times of confucius. although these are in chinese, they do have english subtitles. the confucius temple is one of the most

searchText: dine in style at eiles bistro a family-run italian (and french) bistro tucked near tamsui, with a grand piano and sunday-night performances - fine dining prices, but worth it. eat restaurants fine-dining italian eiles bistro is a great find tucked away near tamsui , close to tamkang university, serving genuinely authentic italian (and some french) cuisine. the owner learnt his trade in italy, and it shows – alongside the usual pasta, lasagne and gnocchi, there are terrific starters, salads and desserts too. it's a lovely, family-run place, decked out with antiques and objects brought over from europe, with a sophisticated, slightly french ambiance. one nice touch: there's a grand piano in the dining room, and regular piano players perform on sunday nights. service is friendly and willing to customise dishes, and there's a large collection of bottled beers and wines to go with your meal. it's rated 4.6 out of 5 on tripadvisor from a solid base of reviews, with the general consensus being a fairly limited menu but excellent quality. it does sway towards fine dining, and the prices reflect that, but it's ultimately worth every dollar – especially if you're already spending the day in tamsui. traveller tips they have good savings when buying three courses and a drink. location 📍 closest mrt: danshui (end of red line - exit 1)

searchText: taiwan traditional theatre centre: opera & tickets a modern 2016-built venue in shilin for traditional beijing opera and chinese orchestral music - first-class performances, even if the dialogue is in chinese. music venues theatre concerts dance if you've a desire to experience traditional chinese and taiwanese theatre and music, the taiwan traditional theatre centre is the place to go. it's run by the national center for traditional arts, at no. 751 wenlin road in shilin – not far from shilin night market . the building itself opened in 2016 and is modern, almost futuristic looking, with a main auditorium spread across two floors of very comfortable seating and a capacity of just over 1,000. the national chinese orchestra of taiwan and the guoguang opera company are both resident here, with the latter staging beijing opera complete with extravagant costumes and makeup, alongside traditional music played on drums, xylophones and other traditional instruments. the dialogue is in chinese, and english surtitles aren't guaranteed – it varies by production, so it's worth checking the listing for the specific show you're interested in. either way, it's the performances and music you should come for. they're first class. traveller tips see their events page for upcoming performances. location 📍 closest mrt: zhishan (red line - exit 1)

title: Huge Range of Whiskeys at The Malt
excerpt: A whisky bar in Da'an with around 500 bottles, started among friends sharing their own collections - now home to Taiwan-exclusive bottlings and an extensive Kavalan range.
searchText: huge range of whiskeys at the malt a whisky bar in da'an with around 500 bottles, started among friends sharing their own collections - now home to taiwan-exclusive bottlings and an extensive kavalan range. drink bars whiskey with one of the largest and most impressive ranges of whiskey in taipei, the malt (麥村) should be the first stop for any whiskey connoisseurs. it started life informally, as a small group of friends sharing their personal whisky collections with each other, before owner hong qi-ming turned it into the bar it is today. around 500 bottles line the shelves, with malts, scotches, bourbons and rye whiskeys gathered from across the world, including many from the uk and ireland, japan and the usa. look out too for the taiwan-exclusive bottlings from the likes of arran, bruichladdich and glenlivet, plus a good showing from taiwan's own acclaimed kavalan distillery and the omar label. unsurprisingly the taiwanese owner is a huge lover of whiskey, and has travelled the world to add to his collection, and imported many others. the whiskeys are sorted by country and price, with the prices varying greatly depending on the rarity and age of the whiskey. there's no menu as such – you browse the shelves, check the price on the back of the bottle (anywhere from around nt$50 to nt$4,000 a glass depending on rarity), and bring your choice to the counter. it really is an almost impossible task to choose one, but the owner and his assistant will do their best to find a suitable one. after you've chosen your desired whiskey, they will bring you a glass of it to your table along with the bottle.

title: Huge Vegetarian Menu at Miacucina
excerpt: A vegetarian restaurant chain with several Taipei branches, serving a broad menu that goes well beyond Italian dishes despite the name.
searchText: huge vegetarian menu at miacucina a vegetarian restaurant chain with several taipei branches, serving a broad menu that goes well beyond italian dishes despite the name. eat restaurants healthy breakfast/brunch italian pizza vegan/vegetarian salads miacucina is a vegetarian restaurant chain with a few branches in taipei. meaning 'my kitchen' in italian, while they do serve a lot of dishes found in italy, their menu includes many other styles of food. the restaurants are nicely fitted out with an urban and modern feel. their neihu branch especially, is one of the nicest places we've dined in taipei. neihu branch miacucina's menu is one of the most extensive in taipei, and it would take dozens of visits to try everything here. it includes: open sandwiches and french toast - inc. honey peanut butter and strawberry ricotta soups - thick western style, inc. squash, carrot & ginger, mushroom mini platters - inc. eggplant and asparagus, roasted corn with blue cheese salads - inc. potato salad, tofu salad, veggie bacon salad 'budda' bowls - veggie bowls with fresh ingredients pasta - inc. lasagne, bolognese and mac 'n' cheese burgers - made with their own veggie patty panini - inc. 3 cheese, pesto, veggie bacon flatbreads - inc. grilled pepper, pesto avocado, roasted tomato a special shout out goes to their budda bowls. the super protein budda bowl we tried was simply divine. everything was fresh and crisp, topped off with a poached egg and a spicy thai peanut sauce. one of the very best we've had in taipei. flatbreads aren't something you find too often in taipei, so we decided upon the western grilled pepper , with grilled corn

title: Eclectic World Music at the Taiwan World Music Festival
excerpt: A three-day world music festival each October at Dajia Riverside Park, with free buses laid on from Xingtian Temple MRT.
searchText: eclectic world music at the taiwan world music festival a three-day world music festival each october at dajia riverside park, with free buses laid on from xingtian temple mrt. culture events festivals live music the taiwan world music festival is an annual 3 day event held in october, showcasing some great eclectic music from around the world. located in dajia riverside park which is in the northern part of taipei and a fair walk from any mrt station. fortunately, the organisers lay on plenty of free buses to and from xingtian temple mrt each day. with two large stages and a tent, plus many other activities and plenty of food and gift stands, there's easily enough going on to keep you entertained. click to enlarge both stages are large and have great sound systems. the island stage is the secondary stage. the main stage is also equipped with a great lighting rig and some large screens. the music tent is where they'll invite guests, including some of the performers to explain their music style and influences, and give you tasters of their music. music styles range from jazz, hip-hop and folk, to the more unconventional style mashups of middle-eastern sounds and techno. every continent is represented, with mexican, eastern european, mongolian and canadian musicians to name a few. taiwan is well represented too, with more traditional aboriginal bands and contemporary performers and djs. check the official site for this year’s line-up tradattack, probably the most famous and popular band in estonia performed here in 2019. fusing traditional estonian folk music with modern rocks style

title: See Taiwan's Best Dance Group at Cloud Gate Theatre
excerpt: Home to Cloud Gate, Taiwan's most acclaimed dance company, in a rebuilt, award-winning building with four performance spaces.
searchText: see taiwan's best dance group at cloud gate theatre home to cloud gate, taiwan's most acclaimed dance company, in a rebuilt, award-winning building with four performance spaces. visit buildings theatre great views dance cloud gate theatre is home to taiwan's most famous and best dance group of the same name. constructed after a fire destroyed the arts foundation warehouse studio, the building has since won architectural awards, including the prestigious far eastern architectural design award. cloud gate theatre features four performing spaces, including a 400 seat main theatre and a 1,000 capacity outdoor space. these will show a mixture of dance, theatre and music events. taiwan's most famous contemporary dance group, cloud gate group will perform here a few times a year and are definitely worth seeing. they have won many international awards and danced at famous venues throughout the world, including sadler's wells in london. we were lucky enough to see them here, and because it's their home venue, it's a much more intimate affair. they'll sometimes even invite you onstage after the performance to take pictures. quite a unique opportunity! there are other dance groups that perform at cloud gate theatre too, along with both traditional and contemporary theatre, including shadow-puppetry. click here to see what's on at the cloud gate theatre the lighting and sounds rigs here are first-rate, and the setting and building itself are worth the visit alone - the theatre is set upon a hill and surrounded by lush greenery. it's worth checking the schedule for cloud gate theatre if you are planning a

title: Taipei Jazz Festival - Free Jazz at Daan Park
excerpt: Taipei's free annual jazz festival, spread across several venues each October and closing at Daan Forest Park. Dates, venues and what to expect.
searchText: taipei jazz festival - free jazz at daan park taipei's free annual jazz festival, spread across several venues each october and closing at daan forest park. dates, venues and what to expect. culture events festivals free live music taipei jazz festival is taipei's annual jazz event , found at various locations and culminating at the daan park forest pavilion over a weekend in october . the festival has locations at these venues around taipei - songshan cultural park dahu park zhongshan mrt station - jazz square taipei expo daan forest park they also have workshops, masterclasses and lectures about jazz, most of which are free. the jazz at songshan cultural park is usually over 3 nights the weekend prior to the main event at daan forest park. while i wouldn't say the jazz here is brilliant, it's still features some nice bands, although the stage is quite small. some of the acts at some of the other locations are nothing special, but the daan event has some world class performers, while being completely free. it runs for three evenings at the pavilion, kicking off at 17:30 or 18:00 and running until 22:00. each day has four or five acts with jazz bands and musicians showcasing their music. the final act of each night is usually a world class performer. in 2019, it featured one of the world's best young guitarists - mateus asato. an absolute virtuoso and easily one of the best guitarist i've seen live. check out the full video of his show at daan park. the pavilion has loads of benches, although these quickly get filled up so if you want to ensure you get one, it's best to arrive before the jazz starts. last

title: TGI Fridays - Better than you Might Expect
excerpt: TGI Fridays in Taipei serves some of the better western comfort food in the city, closer to the US original than you might expect.

title: Cheap but Tasty Vegan Food at Ooh Cha Cha
excerpt: A plant-based cafe with some of the cheapest (and best) western-style vegan food in Taipei, plus smoothies and fresh bowls.
searchText: cheap but tasty vegan food at ooh cha cha a plant-based cafe with some of the cheapest (and best) western-style vegan food in taipei, plus smoothies and fresh bowls. drink cafes healthy breakfast/brunch vegan/vegetarian ooh cha cha is described as a plant-based cafe - offering tasty vegan dishes and great smoothies. it's one of the cheaper places in taipei to try western style vegan food but also one of the best. serving a few varieties of bowls filled with fresh and crunchy vegetables, organic multi-grained rice or quinoa along with various meat-substitutes such as tempah. ooh cha cha is also a good place to bring your laptop. with a few tables upstairs, they also have a large basement area that's ideal for working – see our other favourite cafes to work from . we tried the vietnamese omnipork bowl that had the flavours and smell of vietnamese cuisine. it was very fragrant and fresh, exactly as vietnamese food should be. the vegan burgers definitely hit the mark too. the spicy mango avocado burger - mushroom patty served in a warm wholemeal bun packed with lettuce, avocado and a homemade hot mango sauce. served with a side of thyme coated wedges and a cashew sour cream dip. their ooch bowl , with organic multi-grain rice, quinoa, baked pumpkin, roasted broccoli, tempeh and avocado sauce was as delicious as it was healthy. ooh cha cha is also a good choice for brunch. their tofu scramble, with tempah sausage (although i'd say it's more like bacon), purple onion, pea sprouts, wedges, avocado and a cashew sour cream is great value at nt$240. another one of my favourite dishes here is the c

title: Ducky Restaurant, Taipei: Duck Done Properly
excerpt: A European-leaning restaurant near Zhongxiao Xinsheng known for its duck dishes - tender, precisely plated, with mains around NT$300-450.
searchText: ducky restaurant, taipei: duck done properly a european-leaning restaurant near zhongxiao xinsheng known for its duck dishes - tender, precisely plated, with mains around nt$300-450. eat restaurants italian although it has a fun name, ducky restaurant does serve some serious dishes. it's described as italian but only really has a couple of pasta and risotto dishes on the menu – it leans more broadly european, with a solid range of meat and seafood, and, of course, duck. the meat is cooked very well, tender and succulent, and every plate is dressed with real precision. most mains run nt$300–450, with the steak-frites the priciest thing on the menu at nt$580 – expect to pay around nt$600 for a full meal. if you've got room, the apple crème brûlée (nt$150) is worth saving space for. it's open tuesday to sunday, 11:30–22:30 (closed mondays), with most of the seating downstairs in the basement. traveller tips go for the duck! reservations can be made online directly from this link . location 📍 closest mrt: zhongxiao xinsheng station (blue line - exit 2)

title: La Villa Danshui - A Sublime Italian by the River
excerpt: A two-floor Italian restaurant on the Danshui riverfront, with outdoor seating and river views to match the food.
searchText: la villa danshui - a sublime italian by the river a two-floor italian restaurant on the danshui riverfront, with outdoor seating and river views to match the food. eat restaurants top pick italian outdoor seating salads la villa danshui is a classy italian located in danshui, at the end of the red line. sitting in a prime location next to the danshui river, it's a large restaurant with two floors and some outdoor seating that offers beautiful views of the river. you can order a main course on it's own or as part of a set for an extra nt$100. this will come with soup, bread, dessert and a drink. they have pasta/risotto mains, while also serving meat and fish dishes, although it's the former i would recommend. i've tried the pan fried short-rib with black pepper sauce and in truth, it was nothing special. the pasta and risotto dishes however are excellent. the linguine shrimp, asparagus, garlic with white wine sauce , with fresh pasta is delicious. the saffron risotto with seafood is a rich bowl of al dente risotto still firm to the bite, with shrimp and clams. also on the menu are salads, soups and other appetisers. one of the best and most refined salads i've tried in taipei is the salmon marinated with ginger and orange . a beautiful looking plate that was fresh and light. their mozzarella sticks , caesar salad with parma ham and mixed salad and are also worthy of a mention. one thing we've yet to try are la villa danshui's afternoon tea set. judging by the pictures we've seen they do look good, although you must have a sweet tooth as there isn't a savoury bite in sight. the drinks menu is va

title: Stunningly Original Brunches at Jie Genge
excerpt: A cozy, homely brunch spot near Da'an MRT with just 12 items on the menu, each one carefully considered.
searchText: stunningly original brunches at jie genge a cozy, homely brunch spot near da'an mrt with just 12 items on the menu, each one carefully considered. eat restaurants breakfast/brunch jie genge is a very cozy and homely brunch place located near da-an mrt. with a well thought out interior, it's a inviting brunch spot with a nice ambience and delicious plates of food to match. it offers some of the most original brunches in taipei and with only 12 items on their menu, it focuses on quality rather than quantity. these dished are subdivided into three categories on their menu: sandwiches brunch risotto the sandwiches are not your run-of-the-mill kind. with exotic ingredients such as fried catfish and sauteed kimchi. we chose the pork tenderloin, bacon and spring onion cream cheese , which was topped off with a perfectly cooked fried egg. with the addition of the garnishes, the presentation spot on and the sandwich itself was akin to a posh bacon and egg sandwich - divine. the brunch plates are equally as exotic. beef cheek with curry sauce and duck breast with fig blueberry jam, stewed vegetables, egg and bread . this is the one we chose, with the duck laid out on a bed of scambled egg and perfectly toasted bread. both dishes are picture perfect, finished with finesse with various nibbles and purees. we have yet to try the risottos at jie genge. these too come with an egg, this time poached at exactly 62.5°. aside from the usual teas and coffees, their drink choice is just as creative. hot wine, ginger vinegar and vanilla milkshakes, but it's the smoothies you

title: Try the Original Bubble Tea at Chun Shui Tang
excerpt: The Taichung tea house that claims to have invented bubble tea in 1987 - the real story behind the drink, and what else is on the menu.
searchText: try the original bubble tea at chun shui tang the taichung tea house that claims to have invented bubble tea in 1987 - the real story behind the drink, and what else is on the menu. eat restaurants tea taiwanese chun shui tang is a traditional taiwanese tea house with a genuinely interesting backstory: it opened in taichung on 20 may 1983 (originally as yangmu tea shop), started by liu han-chieh after he saw a barista shaking iced coffee in japan and brought the idea home as hand-shaken iced tea. a few years later, around 1987–88, one of the shop's managers, lin hsiu-hui, added tapioca pearls to a glass of milk tea – creating what became pearl milk tea, or bubble tea. hanlin tea room in tainan makes a rival claim to the same invention, and the two spent ten years fighting it out in court. in 2019, the ruling came back that it didn't actually matter who invented it first, since bubble tea was never a patented product. chun shui tang still proudly claims the title regardless – and whichever side of the argument you land on, this is as close to the source as you'll get. the name means "spring water house". beyond the bubble tea itself, which is noticeably more refined and creamy than what you'll get in most tea houses, the menu covers a full range of traditional food and snacks – rice and noodle dishes, hot pots, radish cake – alongside other teas and juices. traveller tips bubble tea! it's what you're here for, so don't leave without trying it. location over 10 locations. the best ones below: songshan branch (near taipei arena mrt) xinyi branch (near taipei

title: Catch some Sport or a Concert at Taipei Arena
excerpt: Taiwan's premier indoor arena, in Songshan, known locally as the 'Little Egg Dome' - a 15,000+ capacity venue for major concerts and sporting events.
searchText: catch some sport or a concert at taipei arena taiwan's premier indoor arena, in songshan, known locally as the 'little egg dome' - a 15,000+ capacity venue for major concerts and sporting events. visit buildings live sports concerts taipei arena is taiwan's premier indoor venue for sports and concerts. situated in the songshan district on the site of the old taipei municipal baseball stadium, it's a very modern building with a huge sky screen on the front, and a capacity of over 15,000. construction ran from 2001 to 2005, and it's been known locally ever since as 小巨蛋 (xiao ju dan), or "little egg dome" – a nod to its rounded roof, and these days a nickname that distinguishes it from the much larger taipei dome that opened elsewhere in the city in 2023. it boasts a number of concerts, shows and sporting events each year, including gigs from major artists, west-end shows like the lion king, and sport such as tennis, badminton and basketball. seating configuration changes depending on the event – up to 15,350 for arena-style concerts or basketball, dropping to around 10,000 for shows with a proscenium stage, with 48 vip boxes available too. click to enlarge seating plan the taiwan badminton open is held during september, and features some of the top players in the world, including two of the very best from taiwan. click to read about the taiwan badminton open the oec open tennis tournament has some of the world's top female tennis players and is completely free. click to read about the oec open tennis click here to see all the upcoming events at the taipei arena there's also an olympic sized ice r

title: Watch a World Class Band at Legacy Taipei
excerpt: Taipei's mid-size live music venue, filling a gap between small clubs and arenas since 2009 - a single room that books genuinely world-renowned acts.
searchText: watch a world class band at legacy taipei taipei's mid-size live music venue, filling a gap between small clubs and arenas since 2009 - a single room that books genuinely world-renowned acts. culture music venues live music legacy taipei is a music venue located within the huashan 1914 creative park , open since 2009. before it existed, taipei had no real mid-size venue between small clubs and full arenas, forcing promoters to rent out spaces like veterans' halls or school gyms for anything in between – legacy was built specifically to fill that gap, under director arthur chen, a veteran promoter who's also booked acts for taiwan's ho-hai-yan and simple life festivals. it doesn't host a great many gigs each year but when it does, the bands who play are often very good, world renowned acts. the legacy venue is just a single large room with no bar and a capacity of around 1,200 people. the stage setup is usually good, with a great lighting rig and sound quality to match. attracting bands such as foster the people, mumford & sons, neutral milk hotel, the jesus and mary chain, and talented multi-instrumentalists like french kiwi juice, there's always a great crowd of passionate music geeks. click for a list of upcoming acts at legacy taipei often showing local or other asian indie and pop bands too, although i've yet to see any of these. although there is no bar inside, they'll sometimes have temporary stands set up selling beers and basic cocktails. you can take cans purchased elsewhere inside too. legacy has two other venues in taipei and one in taichung. the legacy max (in xinyi) and legacy m

title: National Palace Museum: What to See & How Long to Allow
excerpt: Nearly 700,000 imperial Chinese artefacts spanning 8,000 years. Which galleries to prioritise, how to skip the queues, and how long you actually need.
searchText: national palace museum: what to see & how long to allow nearly 700,000 imperial chinese artefacts spanning 8,000 years. which galleries to prioritise, how to skip the queues, and how long you actually need. visit buildings essential gardens art museum sightseeing bus fun pass top pick if it's a wealth of imperial chinese history and cultural treasures you seek, the national palace museum (國立故宮博物院) in taipei is an absolute must-visit. housing nearly 700,000 rare artifacts spanning over 8,000 years of chinese history—from neolithic jade carvings to qing dynasty imperial porcelain—it ranks alongside the louvre, the british museum, and the metropolitan museum of art as one of the world's premier cultural institutions. history & imperial origins the story of the national palace museum is as dramatic as the treasures it houses. the collection originally belonged to china's emperors and was housed within the forbidden city in beijing. in the 1930s, as war broke out across east asia, the chinese government embarked on a heroic 16-year evacuation, packing thousands of crates of priceless relics and transporting them across mountains and rivers to prevent their destruction or looting. in 1948–1949, amidst the chinese civil war, nearly 3,000 crates containing the finest, rarest pieces of the imperial collection were safely transported across the taiwan strait to taipei. the museum in shilin opened its doors in 1965 to preserve and showcase these magnificent cultural treasures to the world. famous masterpieces & must-see artifacts because the collection is so vast, only around 3,000 to 5,000 items can be displayed at any given time, with exhibits rotating every three to

excerpt: What might be Taipei's best brownies - moist and gooey with a big range of toppings, from banana to cotton candy, at two central branches.
searchText: heavenly desserts at mr brownie what might be taipei's best brownies - moist and gooey with a big range of toppings, from banana to cotton candy, at two central branches. eat dessert shops western mr brownie (or mr brownies) is the best place in taipei for a proper brownie fix. moist, gooey and thoroughly chocolatey, with a huge range of toppings to choose from – expect flavours like banana, cotton candy and strawberry alongside the classics. beyond the brownies themselves, they do a wide range of brownie-adjacent treats – crêpes, ice cream and drinks all built around the same base. if you're after something savoury instead, the cheesy toasties are also worth trying. both branches are small, and reviews mention they can get crowded and a little slow to serve at peak times – worth bearing in mind if you're in a rush, but not enough to put you off. brownie heaven, basically. traveller tips buy a selection of six brownies for a nice saving. locations 📍 ximen branch (closest mrt: ximen blue line exit 1) dunhua branch (closest mrt: zhongxiao dunhua blue line exit 2)

title: Grab some Grub at Ningxia Night Market
excerpt: One of Taipei's oldest and most compact night markets, with 200+ stalls packed into 170 metres, four Michelin-recommended food stalls, and a surprise 2019 visit from Will Smith.
searchText: grab some grub at ningxia night market one of taipei's oldest and most compact night markets, with 200+ stalls packed into 170 metres, four michelin-recommended food stalls, and a surprise 2019 visit from will smith. visit markets free one of the smallest night markets in taipei, ningxia night market tends to specialise in food. it's a compact pedestrian street just 170 metres long, yet somehow crams in over 200 stalls, tracing its roots back to jiancheng roundabout (建成圓環) a short walk away – a recreational park built by the japanese colonial government in 1908 that drew food vendors from the start. when the roundabout later declined after a fire, ningxia road took over as the neighbourhood's go-to night market. because of its size, it's a night market not visited by many tourists but is very popular with the locals. in fact, because it doesn't tend to attract huge crowds, ningxia night market was the one ang lee chose to bring will smith to in october 2019, while the pair were in taipei promoting their film gemini man. smith tried sesame oil chicken and a papaya and watermelon milk, declared bitter melon juice "不好喝" (not tasty) in mandarin, and even had a go on one of the bb gun balloon game stalls. all the locals favourite food can be found here, such as oyster omelettes, fried chicken, or the braised pork and rice, it's a night market you should visit if you want have a more authentic foody experience. there are four michelin recommended food stalls found within ningxia night market, locations of which can be found below: coloured dots match the pins on the map below. fang chia shredded chicken on th

title: Amazing Brunches at The Antipodean Specialty Coffee
excerpt: An Aussie-style brunch spot with what might be the best western breakfast in Taipei, now with several branches beyond its original in Neihu.
searchText: amazing brunches at the antipodean specialty coffee an aussie-style brunch spot with what might be the best western breakfast in taipei, now with several branches beyond its original in neihu. drink cafes top pick breakfast/brunch the antipodean specialty coffee is a great aussie-style breakfast/brunch restaurant which serves (imho) the best western breakfast in taipei. the original branch, a little way out from the centre of taipei in neihu, has proved so popular that they've since opened another one closer to the city. although not actually run by aussies, the taiwanese owners spent many years in melbourne, australia and grew to love the delicious breakfasts and brunches the city had to offer. with it's modern a clean interior the antipodean has a relaxed ambience and very friendly and polite waiters who speak good english. the antipodean specialty coffee's prize dish is their queen's breakfast platter . a huge board that's shared between two, it comes with 'the works'. salmon, halloumi, 2 eggs, avocado, mushroom, ham, baked beans, toast, cherry tomatoes and two greek yogurt muesli topped with seasonal fruits. definitely a dish fit for a queen, and one of the best breakfast plates we've had anywhere in the world. at nt$890, it's one of the most expensive breakfast's we've had too, but it's easily enough for two to feast on. actually, we did opt for their crispy hash browns and scrambled eggs too, as these are the best we've had in taipei. if you don't like some of the ingredients on the queen's breakfast, you can even make your own 'brekkie', choosing any of the ingredients (and more) from this dish. i

title: Watch an Artist at Work at Treasure Hill
excerpt: A hillside artists’ village of rickety huts and studios above the river, with some of the best city views in Taipei. Free to wander.
searchText: watch an artist at work at treasure hill a hillside artists’ village of rickety huts and studios above the river, with some of the best city views in taipei. free to wander. visit parks art exhibitions free walking if you don't mind steps, treasure hill artists' village is a culturally rich little wonderland set on the side of a hill, offering great views of the city at it's peak. with dozens of huts and rickety buildings located on the different levels of the hill, many of which are studios to the local and international artists who work and live here. click to enlarge map the maze-like steep paths and alleys are decorated with street art and installations, with a surprise seemingly around each and every corner. if you peer through some of the windows, you can even see some of the artists busy with their creations. there are usually a few exhibitions on show, some being free, while others requiring a small entry fee. a list of the current ones can be found here . if you do manage to make it to the top of the village, you'll be rewarded with some great views of the city. there are a few cafes located in the artists village, although when we visited it was difficult to get a table. there are however one or two small shops selling drinks and snacks. treasure hill offers a unique experience in taipei, and is a great place to walk around and explore. it doesn't get overly busy here, especially if you visit during a weekday. pros cultural experience like no other cons the few cafes on site get busy many steps to climb price free to walk around. some galleries have an entrance fee. opening hour

title: Huashan 1914 Creative Park: What's On & Full Guide
excerpt: A 1914 wine factory turned arts complex: galleries, craft shops, an independent cinema and live music. What is on, and how to get there.
searchText: huashan 1914 creative park: what's on & full guide a 1914 wine factory turned arts complex: galleries, craft shops, an independent cinema and live music. what is on, and how to get there. visit parks top pick art exhibitions free sightseeing bus built in 1914, huashan 1914 creative park is an old wine factory and grounds which was converted into a creative space in 2007. a number of the old factory warehouses now hold temporary art or other exhibitions, while the park is also home to craft shops, an independent cinema and live music/theatre venues. the park is a great place to walk around, especially if the sun isn't too intense and the rain stays at bay. the 4 hectare area has been well converted, seamlessly mixing the modern areas with the traditional buildings. there are a few nice cafes and restaurants on the site should you need to escape the heat for a while. trio is a cosy cafe located at the front of the park with some nice outdoor seating, while piccola botega is a nice italian. you'll also find many street performers as you walk around the park, with dancers, statuesque characters and comedy routines that kids will love. a map of huashan 1914 creative park click to enlarge huashan map park areas huashan 1914 creative park has two park areas, a small one at the front and a large open park space at the rear. both parks will have special events during most weekends and sometimes during the week. these include markets, concerts, dance shows or promotional events advertising trips abroad or beverages. the quality of these does vary a lot, but they're all free. click here to see what events are on at huashan wareho

title: Taipei Zoo - Guide and Tips to Make the Most of Your Visit
excerpt: Full guide, including map, tips on when to visit, and suggested route for the Maokong Gondola
searchText: taipei zoo - guide and tips to make the most of your visit full guide, including map, tips on when to visit, and suggested route for the maokong gondola visit parks nature essential walking kids fun pass top pick taipei zoo is the largest and one of the best zoos in asia. not only does it have a huge variety of animals, the zoo has been well designed and offers many nice walking areas. most importantly, the animals seem well looked after and their enclosures are large and suitably made to match their native habitats. costing only nt$100 for entry, it's a cheap but fantastic day out which you can combine with a trip on the maokong gondola , a cable car ride high into the mountains. one of the stations for this is inside the zoo. tip : try to visit taipei zoo from tuesday to friday. see my traveller tips section below for reasons. the newest addition to taipei zoo, the pangolin dome , is a nt$390 million, 1.5 hectare structure filled with the flora and fauna of rainforests. with a total area of 165 hectares, if you intend to visit all of the enclosures, it would take you most of the day. a shuttle train is available to quickly take you to another area, including the maokong gondola station. tickets can be purchased at the entrance to the zoo. however, you can use your easycard directly at the turnstile, which in turn will also give you a discount if you decide to ride in a maokong gondola on the same day. free entry to the zoo also comes as part of the taipei fun pass . taipei zoo map click to enlarge zones i've grouped the zones into 3 areas. north (near the main entrance), centre and so

title: Fine Dining at Saffron Fine Indian Cuisine
excerpt: Michelin Bib Gourmand North Indian food in Tianmu - aromatic curries, tandoori and fresh naan, worth the trip even if you're not staying nearby.
searchText: fine dining at saffron fine indian cuisine michelin bib gourmand north indian food in tianmu - aromatic curries, tandoori and fresh naan, worth the trip even if you're not staying nearby. eat restaurants fine-dining indian michelin guide saffron is a great option if you happen to find yourself in tianmu, in the northern part of taipei – and it's earned a michelin guide bib gourmand for doing it well. the restaurant leans north indian, with unique spice blends and a couple of signatures worth ordering specifically: murgh nawabi (chicken curry) and gosht lahori (mutton curry), both made with meat charred in the tandoor. the masala lamb shank, tandoori chicken and kebabs also come recommended, alongside the usual naan and saffron rice, with roti as an alternative. the dining room has a genuine fine-dining feel – terracotta floors, textured walls, burgundy lanterns and dark wood furniture – with elegant cutlery and plating to match. it's rated 4.5 stars on opentable for consistent cooking and warm service. it's a fair way from any mrt station, so it's really one for those already staying up that end of the city, or willing to make the trip for michelin-recognised north indian food. expect to pay accordingly – this isn't a cheap meal, but the naan bread alone might be some of the best in taipei. traveller tips the naan bread is some of the best in taipei. location 📍 closest mrt: mingde (red line)

title: Tajine Moroccan - Authentic Moroccan Meals
excerpt: Tajine Moroccan is one of only a handful of Moroccan restaurants in Taipei, but it's also one of the best. The owner and chef of Tajine Moroccan is himself Moroccan, and it shows in the authenticity of the dishes. Specia
searchText: tajine moroccan - authentic moroccan meals  eat restaurants moroccan tajine moroccan is one of only a handful of moroccan restaurants in taipei, but it's also one of the best. the owner and chef of tajine moroccan is himself moroccan, and it shows in the authenticity of the dishes. specialising in tajines, they come served with a choice of either saffron rice, couscous or pitta bread. since lamb is the meat often associated with moroccan food, i had to try the traditional lamb tajine . my girlfriend, being a seafood lover chose the lemon seafood tajine . the lamb meat must have been stewed for some time, as it was very tender. i also loved the soft potatoes in my tajine and the kick from the spices. the prawns and fish in the seafood tajine were also perfectly cooked and tasted very fresh. the restaurant no doubt benefits from the taipei fish market, which isn't too far from the songshan restaurant. the warm pitta bread and couscous were a perfect accompaniment to the tajines, allowing us to soak up the delicious sauces. we paid nt$120 each to get a drink and dessert, which is especially worth getting if you want a drink, as these cost at least this amount on their own. we chose the moroccan mint tea and mint lemon juice . for desserts, we chose the orange blossom yogurt and almond cake . while they were both quite small, they were both delicious. in fact, everything we tried at tajine moroccan was delicious. we've yet to try another moroccan re

title: Matcha Saro - Green Tea Desserts to Savour
excerpt: A matcha dessert chain with branches across Taipei's mall food halls, serving Taiwanese-Japanese green tea sweets.
searchText: matcha saro - green tea desserts to savour a matcha dessert chain with branches across taipei's mall food halls, serving taiwanese-japanese green tea sweets. eat dessert shops taiwanese 108 matcha saro (一〇八抹茶茶廊) started life in 2013 as a passion project among friends in asahikawa, hokkaido, before matcha dessert expert yamamoto-san brought the brand to taiwan in 2014. it's since become a fixture in taipei's shopping mall food halls, with several branches serving up its kyoto-sourced matcha desserts and ice-cream. as the name suggests, most of the menu is flavoured with matcha (green tea), a favourite among locals, though hojicha (roasted tea) versions show up too. there are many different ice-creams to choose from (all containing matcha of course), with red beans, jellies and other delights carefully placed inside or on top. their other speciality is the matcha pancake – really an imagawayaki, a japanese filled cake cooked in a special mould rather than a flat pancake, warm and stuffed with matcha custard or red bean. they're all freshly made and ooze goodness. matcha saro is a must for addicts of green tea. it's slightly on the expensive side and the english level among staff is low (though the menu does have english on it), but they deliver on quality and flavour across all three of their locations. traveller tips the imagawayaki pancakes are a must! locations 📍 taipei main q square basement (closest mrt: taipei main) xinyi eslite (closest mrt: taipei city hall) shilin mall basement (closest mrt: mingde)

title: Chiang Kai-Shek Memorial Hall: What to See & Guard Times
excerpt: The changing of the guard times, what to see across Liberty Square, and how long to allow. Free to enter, and one of the few Taipei sights worth timing.
searchText: chiang kai-shek memorial hall: what to see & guard times the changing of the guard times, what to see across liberty square, and how long to allow. free to enter, and one of the few taipei sights worth timing. visit buildings essential gardens art free sightseeing bus top pick the chiang kai-shek memorial hall is a shrine to the former president of the republic of china. situated within liberty square , a huge open expanse covering over 24 hectares, it also boasts the national performance halls, along with the gate of integrity and some beautiful gardens and trails. two ceremonies are performed on the memorial hall site. both the changing of the guards and the flag ceremony come highly recommended. click to enlarge map of liberty square chiang kai-shek chiang kai-shek was a chinese military leader and politician who served as the leader of mainland china between 1928 and 1949, and then of taiwan until his death in 1975. a highly divisive figure in taiwan, chiang kai-shek is both hated and revered here. on the one hand, he helped china overcome the japanese threat in 1945. but his authoritative rule spanning almost 40 years (known as the 'white terror'), plus his apparent role in the 28 february massacre, have left many with a very bitter taste in their mouth. memorial hall the huge memorial hall was erected in chiang kai-shek's honour a year after his death, in 1976. constructed using mainly concrete and marble, the 89 steps leading up to the bronze statue hall represent the number of years he was alive. the hall features a large statue of the former leader and is guarded by two military personnel. changing of the guards every hour between 09:00 and

title: Healthy and Tasty Brunches at Tamed Fox
excerpt: A healthy, easy-on-the-waistline brunch spot with a large communal sharing table. Come outside peak hours for a table to yourselves.

title: Authentic Thai Cuisine at Home's Thai
excerpt: Home's Thai have a couple of branches in Taipei which serves some great authentic Thai food. With two branches in Taipei, the Songshan branch is a lot less formal than the Fuxing Road branch - which is aimed at the many
searchText: authentic thai cuisine at home's thai  eat restaurants thai home's thai have a couple of branches in taipei which serves some great authentic thai food. with two branches in taipei, the songshan branch is a lot less formal than the fuxing road branch - which is aimed at the many businesses in this area. we often try the shrimp pancakes as a test for the authenticity and tastiness of a thai restaurant. the ones at home's thai are juicy and packed with shrimp flavour. if you like your thai food especially spicy, homes thai will not disappoint, as most of their dishes do not hold back on the heat. even the vegetable dishes are infused with chilli heat. the tom yam soups are especially spicy, while the pad thai is very authentic, being exactly as they are in thailand. they have all the usual thai dishes, and include some nice fish dishes on the menu - the lemongrass sea-bass is probably the most popular, while the tempura-like soft-shell crab with lemongrass is a complex flavour sensation. the crispy chicken, with soy sauce and infused with garlic, chillis and spring onion is another great dish. the service is also very good, with friendly staff and a nice atmosphere. home's thai is one of our favourite places for thai food and is one to try especially if you love spicy food. menu visit their website menu page . pros very spicy (although you can ask to tone it down) generally no waiting to be seated authentic cons slightly expensive price:

title: Huge Western Menu at Gordon Biersch
excerpt: A German-inspired American chain with four branches in central Taipei, known for its craft ales alongside a big western menu.
searchText: huge western menu at gordon biersch a german-inspired american chain with four branches in central taipei, known for its craft ales alongside a big western menu. eat restaurants western craft beer live sports salads gordon biersch is a german inspired american restaurant chain with four branches in the taipei city centre. originally based in california, it has since expanded around the globe and is known for creating some fine craft ales and delicious western food. as far as i'm aware, gordon biersch have never opened a branch in the uk so i was unfamiliar with their brand, and keen to sample some of the ales and food. gordon biersch have a range of beers, from light to very dark and includes hoppy, fruity and malty variations. if you want to try one of each without getting too tipsy, they have flights which can be purchased together. food-wise, gordon biersch have one of the largest range of western dishes in taipei, with many salads, burgers, pasta, pizza, seafood, tacos, ribs and steaks. as with all the western chains in taipei, you will tend to pay more than you would normally in the west, but their burgers, steaks and pasta dishes especially as some of the best i've had in taipei. gordon biersch also have one of the best dessert menus i've seen in taipei, which includes cheesecakes, brownies, ice-cream and a selection of other fine cakes. these are rich and indulgent and are ideal for those with an especially sweet tooth. if you're visiting during october, gordon biersch has their own oktoberfest which includes discounted food and drinks menus. menu visit their extensive menu pages on

title: Very Thai - Refined and Delicious Thai Dishes
excerpt: An upmarket Thai restaurant chain with several branches, related to the cheaper Thai Town and the noodle-focused Very Thai Noodles.
searchText: very thai - refined and delicious thai dishes an upmarket thai restaurant chain with several branches, related to the cheaper thai town and the noodle-focused very thai noodles. eat restaurants thai very thai is an upmarket thai restaurant chain with a number of conveniently located branches that serves some of our favourite thai food in taipei. the same company also owns the very thai noodles chain (also very good) and the slightly cheaper thai town, but it's worth the extra money to come here instead. a starter we always enjoy here is the shrimp pancakes with sweet chilli sauce. they advertise it as their number one signature dish, and with reason. a perfect start to any thai meal. it's difficult for us to eat at any thai restaurant without trying the pad thai , on the menu as thai-style fried rice noodles - and very thai do a great one. very pad thai! another of their signature dishes is the tom yam soup . juicy pieces of shrimp in a hot and sour soup, it's very spicy but just as delicious. thai curries are another of our favourites, and it's sometimes difficult to choose between the red, green and yellow variants. this time we chose the green curry , again laced with chilli heat but creamy and rich. their selection is very large, and very authentic. the thai style shrimp fried rice dish, with spring onions and egg is as delicious as it sounds. dishes generally cost between nt$200 and nt$350, although the sea-bass will set you back around nt$600. they also have a number of beverages, both alcoholic and non-alcoholic. their beer selection is extensive and includes a numb

title: Very Thai Noodles - Comforting Bowls of Goodness
excerpt: A quick-service spin-off of Very Thai, serving Thai and Vietnamese-inspired noodle dishes for a fast, hearty meal.
searchText: very thai noodles - comforting bowls of goodness a quick-service spin-off of very thai, serving thai and vietnamese-inspired noodle dishes for a fast, hearty meal. eat restaurants thai quick eats very thai noodles is a spin-off restaurant of the excellent very thai restaurants, with an aim to bring quick and hearty food. they specialise in thai/vietnamese inspired ramen-style dishes but offer dry noodles and rice dishes too. service here is fast, so if you're in a hurry but looking for something delicious, this is a good option. the standard and consistency of the dishes is very good., with the broths being deep and rich in flavour and the accompanying meat or fish cooked nicely. the tom yam kung noodles , with a choice of pork, seafood or both is rich with a bold taste. the thai style curry noodles with chicken drumstick is hearty, creamy and delicious. the only issue you'll have is the mess you will no doubt make, attempting to eat them with spoon and chopsticks. they do however provide bibs to contain any splash-back. you could also choose a safer option - the minced pork on a bed of rice with a deep-fried and battered egg on top and plenty of chilli. splash-back free! they also have ice-cream to take away which comes in two flavours - matcha and sesame - both excellent. there are many locations dotted in and around taipei, one is right before the security check at departures in songshan airport. very thai noodles is a great choice whether you're in a hurry or just fancy something comforting yet delicious! pros many locations quick service cons limited choice price:

searchText: get wooed by the cocktails at woo taipei (permanently closed)    permanent closure notice please note: woo taipei has permanently closed. woo taipei is a stylish and popular bar and restaurant that specialises in wines and cocktails, while serving some great western dishes. the large main room is decked out with old wooden furniture, cast-iron stoves and many filament light bulbs which are the only light-sources in this dimly lit environment. with the sounds of smooth cool music and the buzz of chat, woo taipei has a great atmosphere. the wine list is extensive, and there are many fine cocktails to choose from, each with their own twist. their "we'll make you woo" cocktails are precisely crafted alcoholic works-of-art. the food choice is also good, with english style pub food like fish and chips, plenty of pasta options, and a variety of food to share such as tapas and seafood platters. we particularly enjoyed their garlic shrimp & mushrooms in taiwan beer . woo taipei is a great bistro style bar that usually gets busy over the weekend. you may need to queue to get in, but you'll have a great time once inside. pros great atmosphere high quality cocktails cons quite expensive expect to queue to get in during peak hours price: $$$ level of english: good (english on menu) traveller tips the food platters are great sharing options location 📍 closest mrt: zhongxiao dunhua (blue line)

title: Watch the Footy at The Brass Monkey
excerpt: An established western bar popular with American expats, built around watching live sport on a projector and multiple screens.
searchText: watch the footy at the brass monkey an established western bar popular with american expats, built around watching live sport on a projector and multiple screens. eat drink bars western craft beer pool table live sports one of the more established western bars in taipei, the brass monkey is a popular destination for american ex-pats and tourists. it's one of the best venues to watch live sport , with a projector in the back room and numerous tvs, and show a very wide range of sports including: premier & champions league football f1 and moto gp boxing and ufc nba & afl the brass monkey also has a good selection of draft lagers and real ales, and have a couple of great happy hour deals. from 11:00 - 20:00 each day, you can get draft lagers, beers, bottles and spirits from around nt$100. they also have a new monkey hour between 17:00 and 18:00, where many of these are reduced to nt$90 including house wines. brass monkey serve largely portioned western dishes that are some of the best in taipei. i've not had better pies or fish & chips anywhere else in taipei. this is the smaller sized version which is plenty for me but they have a large portion too. if you're visiting over the christmas period, this is the place to come for a great meal. turkey, stuffing, mash, veg, sausages, gravy and cranberry sauce. probably the best christmas meal in taipei. the room towards the rear also has a large pool table that's free to play, and for large sporting events they'll pull down a screen here for the projector. brass monkey is usually a lively place to enjoy a drink, especially when taipei plays host to large

title: On Tap - The Most Authentic British Pub in Taiwan
excerpt: Billed as Taipei's only authentic British pub, with draft ales and walls covered in British memorabilia. What's on tap and the vibe.
searchText: on tap - the most authentic british pub in taiwan billed as taipei's only authentic british pub, with draft ales and walls covered in british memorabilia. what's on tap and the vibe. eat drink bars western craft beer pool table live sports outdoor seating billed as taipei's only real pub, on tap is the most authentic british style bar in taipei, serving draft lagers and ales, plus a variety of pub food. the walls are plastered with british memorabilia, with union flags, london buses and numerous icons from british pop and film culture. it's probably the closest you'll come to feeling like your drinking in an english pub in taipei. consisting of two levels, the ground level includes plenty of outdoor seating (only until 22:00 though), while the basement has a free pool table, darts and other games such as jenga. if you're after live sport , on tap is the best place to come in taipei. with no less than 14 screens, 3 of them projectors, they have the ability to show multiple sporting events simultaneously. although, much like other venues, they will only turn the sound up for the largest events such as the football world cup or the wimbledon final. the beer selection at on tap is very good, and includes a few very british badger ales and some belgian lagers, and they have some decent tap ales, including taiwan's own redpoint. the drinks menu is extensive to say the least, with bottled and canned beers/ciders as well as the drafts ones, wines, whiskeys, cocktails, shots, bombs and soft drinks. there is a wide variety of pub food to choose from, and it's generally of a good standard. almost everything you'll find in a pub in britain

title: Perfect English Afternoon Tea at Smith & Hsu
excerpt: The most authentic English afternoon tea in Taipei, according to a Brit who's had plenty of the real thing back home.
searchText: perfect english afternoon tea at smith & hsu the most authentic english afternoon tea in taipei, according to a brit who's had plenty of the real thing back home. eat restaurants tea afternoon tea sandwiches if you crave an afternoon tea whilst in taipei, look no further than smith & hsu . they serve the most authentic afternoon tea in taipei. this is coming from a brit who has had many an afternoon tea in the english towns around the country. smith & hsu is a match for many i've had. you can purchase a tea set for one , which consists of a tea and scones with clotted cream and jam. the scones are without question the best i've tried in taiwan. soft and moist on the inside with a firm exterior, although perhaps i'd like a larger portion of cream and jam. if you're here as a pair, then i'd recommend going for the lady smith afternoon tea set or the queen victoria afternoon tea set . these come with the scones and tea, with the addition of 6 sandwiches, one jelly each and cake (the queens will come with 2 cakes and cookies). when we were there, the sandwiches consisted of ham salad smoked salmon and capers beef and tomato all were delectable and worthy of any english tea set. we chose the earl grey cheesecake, which was soft and creamy, with the taste of tea to match our beverages. you can choose from around 30 teas, which they'll bring samples for you to sniff at your table. these range from fine english teas, fruit teas, oolong, and more unusual ones such as black chocolate mint tea. at a cost of just over nt$1,100 with the service charge, the lady smith is probably a similar prici
